Sports.title: Mamardashvili saves penalty as Georgia hold Northern Ireland in Nations League
Sports.content:
It is a sign of Northern Ireland’s progress that irritation was writ large across the faces of players, supporters and the manager, Michael O’Neill, as scoreless parity was confirmed. This youthful team had already emerged as one of the fascinating tales of the Nations League.

That they were unable to breach Georgia, even with a late penalty, understandably stung, yet this has been a hugely positive window. They emerge unbeaten and atop their group. In a nod to the exertions of a four-game spell this early in the season, plus heavy travel in Northern Ireland’s case, exhaustion was obvious long before full time.

The difficulty here related to a rising wave of expectation. The superb performance during Friday’s 3-0 win over Ukraine backed up victory away to Georgia and a draw with Hungary. O’Neill’s men were yet to concede a goal in this section. A team quietly tipped to peak around qualification for Euro 2028 was blossoming earlier than anticipated, and this without the long-term absentee Conor Bradley. Northern Ireland’s oldest starter for Georgia’s visit was the 28-year-old Ciaron Brown. The partners for Brown in a three-man back line were 20 and 21.

Georgia are a curious case, ranked outside the world’s top 70 yet containing one of its finest players. Clearly Khvicha Kvaratskhelia cannot carry a nation on his own. Indeed, the superstar’s first act was to pass the ball straight to Ethan Galbraith in the Northern Ireland midfield. During the nondescript early exchanges, Kvaratskhelia also gifted possession to Jamie Donley.

What football existed in the first half came from the hosts. Ruairi McConville, one of those fresh-faced centre-backs, came closest to opening the scoring with a header from Justin Devenny’s cross, Giorgi Mamardashvili not at all convincing in denying him. Georgia responded, an excellent save from Pierce Charles necessary to deny Zuriko Davitashvili. The let-off triggered a sweeping Northern Ireland move which culminated in Devenny over-hitting a low cross. Northern Ireland were frustrated by the wasting of umpteen set plays during the first period.

That Davitashvili moment aside, Georgia offered nothing in an attacking sense. Northern Ireland should have edged ahead four minutes before the interval, Patrick Kelly instead fluffing his lines having evaded the Georgia defence from Trai Hume’s through ball.

View image in fullscreen Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was kept relatively quiet, but even so came close to scoring a fantastic goal. Photograph: Cathal McNaughton/Reuters

Kelly appeared in two minds over whether to shoot or play in a teammate, and the visitors seized upon his indecision. The half ended with Isaac Price curling a free-kick into the wrong side of the Georgian side-netting. This rather summed up 45 minutes of promise and no punch from those in green.

Price, born in Yorkshire, epitomises Northern Ireland’s diligence in sourcing players available through bloodline eligibility. The Manchester-born Charles brothers – Shea, the captain, was once again classy in midfield as Pierce kept goal – do likewise. This is, however, no team pulled together from afar; Galbraith was once a boy wonder in Belfast before being coaxed to Manchester United as a teenager. His imaginative playmaking will surely one day be worthy of a grander stage than Stoke and the Championship.

This big-picture stuff was irrelevant as Georgia stood firm. On a rare counterattack, Pierce Charles was called into action to collect a deflected shot from the substitute Giorgi Tsitaishvili. This was a game of chess, a game of intrigue, where Northern Ireland were superior while lacking a ruthless touch. Georgia’s threat was understated but real.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Galbraith limped off with 25 minutes to play, in what constituted an obvious blow to O’Neill. The game by now was tense and scrappy. While against better opponents that may have suited Northern Ireland, that was patently not the case this time. Georgia were managing to sap energy from the home support.

With fatigue apparent across the pitch, O’Neill turned to a 36-year-old who plies his club trade at Stevenage to beef up the attack. Josh Magennis edges ever close to 100 caps, with this No 93.

Kvaratskhelia had been strangely subdued for 79 minutes, but striding forward from midfield, the Paris Saint-Germain forward cracked a 20-yard drive just over the crossbar. What a goal it would have been if a touch lower.

Magennis was handed a golden chance but Mamardashvili saved. A melee from the subsequent corner saw the crossbar struck but, more significantly, the video assistant referee’s attention drawn to a kick in the face of McConville by Budu Zivzivadze. A spot-kick was correctly awarded. Up stepped Price, whose penalty was saved, low to his right, by Mamardashvili. Had Northern Ireland passed up their moment? As Shea Charles curled wide, they had. Georgia, themselves weary, stood firm.

Sports.title: Police occupy Djibouti FA headquarters amid attempt to oust Fifa council member
Sports.content:
Attempts to oust Souleiman Waberi as the president of the Djibouti football federation (FDF) reached a dramatic climax on Monday as police occupied the federation’s headquarters after a group of club presidents called an extraordinary general assembly aimed at removing the Fifa council member and his executive committee.

The FDF said police first occupied its national technical centre at about 5.30pm on Sunday, without presenting an administrative document or court order. According to the federation, on Monday a much larger police contingent ordered Waberi, members of the executive committee, staff and other federation members to leave the premises.

The FDF said 16 club presidents then entered the building under police escort and proceeded to hold what it described as a “purported” EGM. The federation rejected the meeting as illegitimate, saying it had not been properly convened and that the notice periods and procedures required under its statutes and electoral code had not been respected. It declared any decisions taken “null and void”. But sources in Djibouti have insisted the number of delegates required by the statutes was present. They unanimously voted to remove Waberi and the executive committee before establishing an interim committee to oversee the federation.

Quick Guide How do I 

The confrontation follows weeks of mounting opposition to Waberi, a member of the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee as well as Fifa’s council and a close ally of Gianni Infantino. At the start of September, a coalition of 27 clubs announced its intention to vote on the removal of the executive committee and insisted it had secured the two-thirds support required under the federation’s statutes.

The FDF disputed that calculation, saying it has 67 members and that 45 – not 27 – would be required to trigger an extraordinary assembly. The dispute escalated as additional clubs and delegates joined the campaign against the executive committee. The government then intervened, with the secretary of state for sport, Fatouma Ali Abdallah, ordering the FDF to convene an extraordinary general assembly within 72 hours.

The FDF has appealed to Fifa and Caf, arguing that the use of state security forces to remove elected officials could constitute interference in the affairs of a national football association. It warned that the consequences could include suspension, exclusion of Djiboutian clubs and national teams from international competitions, and a freeze on development programmes and funding. The Guardian has requested a comment from Fifa.

It is understood Waberi and several other officials could be facing charges this week after a police investigation of the FDF related to suspected embezzlement and money laundering was completed. They were arrested in September 2024 after a government inspection of the FDF identified financial and administrative irregularities, including weaknesses in procurement, cash management and financial controls. The government’s investigation also raised concerns about anomalies in payments to third parties, failure to pay tax on salaries and wages and “misuse of cash payments” totalling almost £500,000. The police then carried out its investigation.

Waberi has denied wrongdoing. He said in August after the FDF was accused by a club official of misusing funds that Fifa’s “monitoring mechanisms have revealed no indication of wrongdoing regarding the funds it disbursed”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fifa, which along with Caf contributes more than $1m (£760,000) a year to the FDF through its forward development programme, has financed football infrastructure and youth-development programmes in Djibouti, including the Douda academy and artificial-pitch projects in Arta and Dikhil. But it is understood that various tenders are under investigation because they did not comply with standard procedures.

Several foreign workers who were not in compliance with immigration regulations were sent back to their home countries, meaning construction was halted. According to several Caf and Fifa employees and contractors, the projects in Djibouti are “a complete farce”. “We pass on the information but nothing happens,” said one contractor. “The money has gone missing, the projects are never finished – or if they are, it’s just a bare-bones version – and nobody says a word. It breaks my heart for the young people who just want to play football.”

Sports.title: Ronaldo’s break with Portugal is sad, fitting, and long overdue | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
If this is to be the end for Cristiano Ronaldo at international level, at least it can be said that he left the stage as he bestrode it: with monumental self-regard. Ronaldo has always been a preening, self-absorbed player, but for a time, when he was one of the best in the world, it could be tolerated. For the past four years, though, he has actively and obviously held Portugal back. There is a great generation of technical talent here weighed down by the monstrous albatross of his ego.

To recap the basic details of the past couple of weeks. Ronaldo played 67 minutes of Portugal’s scratchy 1-0 win over Wales. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, who replaced Roberto Martínez after the World Cup, said he had a verbal agreement with Ronaldo that he would not start the following game against Norway but would perhaps come off the bench. Early in the second half, Ronaldo went to warm up – although whether that was on his own initiative or because Jesus had told him to is unclear. The game was tight, Portugal ultimately winning 2-1, and Jesus did not bring Ronaldo on.

To Ronaldo and his army of apologists, Jesus was guilty of an unacceptable provocation. Jesus’s view was that winning the game took priority over the extremely delicate feelings of a 41-year-old forward. Ronaldo walked out on the squad, and perhaps on his international career, although only three days later, seemingly after Jesus had refused to pay penance for his blasphemy. Which is sad, although perhaps not quite in the way Ronaldo thinks it is.

It’s possible Jesus, who also coached Ronaldo at Al Nassr, could have handled the situation differently. He is not, it’s fair to say, a diplomat. After Martínez’s soft-pedalling, that is, though, perhaps exactly what was needed. Jesus is 72. His vision of management is old-school, which is to say that he is a dictator and he takes orders only from the club president, and then only if he feels like it. His career has been characterized by rifts with players who have resisted him. In a sense the only surprise is that his falling out with Ronaldo took until the second game of his reign.

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo was left on the sidelines against Norway. Photograph: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/Shutterstock

Others might have been cowed in the face of Ronaldo’s sulk, the online backlash and criticism from some of the Portuguese press, certain elements of which Ronaldo owns, but not Jesus. He is a man of great eloquence and is always quotable but, even by his standards, his response to the furore has been remarkable as he has insisted on the primacy of the team over any individual. “I can say to any player that you’re starting on the bench: if I need you for 30 minutes you’re going to play, if I don’t need you, you’re not going to play,” he said. “The way I was reading the game he didn’t come on. Because it’s not Cristiano, just like it will never be any player that will change my ideas as the coach. Never! Not him, not anyone in football. Not him, not anyone, not any president. Never! Zero!”

His hardline approach might have backfired had Portugal then lost to Denmark, but they won 4-2, playing superbly. Gonçalo Ramos, who might have thought he had already settled this argument by replacing Ronaldo at the 2022 World Cup for the last-16 game against Switzerland and scoring a hat-trick in a 6-1 win, set up the first and scored another against the Danes, having already scored the winner against Norway. “The new manager is a great help,” Ramos said. “We have clearer ideas; we know exactly where each teammate is, both in defense and attack. We’re improving day by day, and it’s all part of a process. We’re very happy with the win, once again against a good team.” Ramos was on target Sunday as Portugal came from behind to beat Norway at home, making it four wins out of four in this window.

The tendency until now has been for the other Portugal players to back Ronaldo, to insist he was an icon and that they didn’t mind his superannuated lumbering. Bruno Fernandes has been notably diplomatic, but others are starting to break cover. Ramos’s former Paris Saint-Germain teammate Vitinha, for instance, who has seen at club level how beneficial a purge of egos can be, observed that Portugal’s improvement has been “the work of the coach … I think beyond the win, the content of our game was great.”

Jesus has offered Ronaldo another meeting to try to resolve the situation, but the Portuguese football federation seems already to have accepted how the affair will end, beginning plans for a farewell game for the country’s record scorer. Both Jesus and Ronaldo have indicated they will say more this week.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But the truth is that this is a break that should have happened long ago. For three tournaments, Ronaldo has undermined an extremely talented Portugal. This is a sad story. It is sad Ronaldo’s career should have ended this way. But the saddest element is that a great player could be so deluded about his own fading ability that a national team’s hopes and dreams should have been sacrificed to his quest to break goalscoring records.

Sports.title: WSL talking points: heat cranks up on Arsenal and Putellas and Diani shine
Sports.content:
1 Fans stay connected to Slegers

Travelling Arsenal fans showed no animosity towards the head coach, Renée Slegers, despite their side’s run of one win in six games in all competitions and slipping 10 points behind Manchester City. Slegers walked over to applaud the 2,000 away fans after the 4-2 defeat at Etihad Stadium, on Sunday and they applauded her back. Slegers said: “I mostly went there to thank them, connect with them and show them I care for them and appreciate them coming to Manchester. And also to show them that I feel – not sorry for them because I’m a big part of it and things are within my control – but they’re coming here and they’re not getting the rewards, just like the team. I wanted to connect with them instead of walking away and hiding.” Tom Garry

View image in fullscreen Lauren Hemp celebrates scoring Manchester City’s third goal. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

2 Forward-thinking Walsh lifts Chelsea

Chelsea’s midfield came to the fore again in their 3-0 win over West Ham. Keira Walsh was the heartbeat of the team, collecting her third straight player of the match award with the 29-year-old enjoying a more attacking role this season. With the introduction of Lexi Potter at half-time, Walsh was able to push forward fruitfully again. She scored her second WSL goal of 2026-27 – the same as she managed last season – and took more shots (five) and completed more dribbles (three) than anyone else. “It helps us a lot in terms of creating opportunities,” said her coach, Sonia Bompastor. “We know how good she is at the edge of the box … It’s good to have a player who is confident and brings us the solution to scoring goals.” Sophie Downey

3 Lionesses flex their muscles

London City showed their Champions League qualification credentials with a 6-1 rout of Tottenham to move above them into third. They were at their fluid and clinical best against a team many believe will rival them as challengers to the traditional top three, with 47.6% of shots on target compared with Tottenham’s 11%. Superstar signings Alexia Putellas and Kadidiatou Diani both scored twice, but most impressive was the muscle the squad showed. They looked more robust and hungrier than Tottenham, their physical presence combined with an aggressive press making the home team look pedestrian and lightweight despite an unbeaten start to the season. With lots of summer changes it can take time for players to gel and that physical presence can make a difference when things aren’t clicking. When things are clicking, though, it appears anything is possible. Suzanne Wrack

4 Pointless Charlton neglect basics

The Charlton manager, Karen Hills, did not mince her words after her side conceded five despite taking the lead at Brighton. “It’s unacceptable if we can’t deal with one v ones,” she said. “The game is about one v one duels, about tackling, doing the basics and doing them really well. Unfortunately, we didn’t do that today. We found ourselves on the end of the scoreline which isn’t very flattering for us. We need to be more accountable for some individual stuff, but at the same time I take full responsibility because that’s my team out there.” The international break comes at a critical time for the team, who are yet to pick up a point. Even with some time to work on their unacceptable handling of the basics, it is hard to where Charlton’s first point is coming from. SW

5 Liverpool unsuccessfully copy United

Gareth Taylor admitted surprise at Manchester United’s directness after his Liverpool team succumbed to a 1-0 defeat at Leigh Sports Village. Possession was split almost evenly, with 51% for Liverpool, and the hosts created more goalmouth opportunities, but could not convert them. Taylor told the BBC: “We ended up becoming what they are, very direct. We have got to be braver – and do what we do.” TG

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Julia Zigiotti Olme of Manchester United (left) celebrates after her goal settled the match against Liverpool. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

6 Familiar problems for Sørensen at Villa

Brian Sørensen’s first WSL game as Aston Villa’s interim manager ended in a 1-1 draw with Crystal Palace. The Dane took over on Tuesday after Natalia Arroyo’s dismissal, with Villa having won two points from their opening four league matches. Villa took the lead through Noelle Maritz in the 55th minute, but Abbie Larkin’s equaliser 19 minutes later ensured Villa remain without a league win. Villa were fortunate not to concede again as Palace’s confidence grew and created several chances late on, and the draw leaves them 12th. Villa and Sørensen have work to do, whether his appointment remains temporary or becomes permanent. Réshma Rao

7 Mace ends Everton’s goal wait

It was quite a feat for Everton to be in the top five without registering anything other than an own goal and their luck continues. They finally scored goals of their own in a 2-1 victory against Birmingham. It was all thanks to Ruby Mace, who scored them both. Her most recent WSL goal came playing for the visitors in 2021. The first was a stunning left-foot strike into the far corner; the second a deflected shot from the edge of the area. “I’m really happy. I have [been working on my shooting], putting in the extra work, and luckily today I managed to score,” she said. Renuka Odedra

Sports.title: Celtic celebrate heated win over Rangers in final of revived Tennent’s Sixes
Sports.content:
The intensity of the football rivalry in Glasgow was evident on Sunday night as Celtic turned the tables on Rangers to win the Tennent’s Sixes. Celtic beat their rivals 5-4 in the final at Braehead Arena after being on the end of a 7-1 defeat by Rangers in the group stage on Saturday.

The tournament was for retired players from all 12 Premiership teams as the SPFL revived a tournament that took place between first teams from 1984 to 1993. But the reactions were similar to any major trophy final.

Celtic’s Charlie Mulgrew admitted he got carried away in his celebrations after he ignored handshake attempts from the Rangers captain, Andy Halliday, in order to salute the crowd, and exchanged words with the Rangers manager, Barry Ferguson.

There was a heated post-match analysis in the Rangers dressing room. In a video leaked on social media, Kirk Broadfoot appears to be heavily criticising the goalkeeper Lee Robinson.

Mulgrew had calmed only slightly when he spoke to Premier Sports. “A lot of adrenaline was flowing, a few nasty tackles,” the 40-year-old said. “I mean, I know it was the Tennent’s Sixes, but you get caught up in the moment.

“You don’t like to get beat from Rangers, our closest rivals, 7-1, so that hurt. We had a few beers, a wee chat, a wee night out, so we managed to turn it around. We got a few things ironed out, although I was a wee bit rough in the morning.

“It feels like I’ve won an actual, real cup. It’s mental. I got a bit carried away at the end there but it builds up. There was a lot of emotion in that. Sometimes that’s what happens, it spills over.

“Football’s like that. I got nutmegged a couple of times by [Martyn] Waghorn, and exchanged words with him, then that was me. I was just fired up and fired into a few tackles. In the end, because we had that spirit, we won.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Celtic’s manager, Tom Boyd, said he was “pretty angry” with his players on Saturday night and that it “feels like winning the league”.

His assistant, Simon Donnelly, admitted they were all “embarrassed” by Saturday’s heavy defeat and told Celtic Player after the final: “It’s against Rangers, so it’s as if it’s a Scottish Cup final there. That’s the feeling. You could play Rangers at tiddlywinks and you’d still want to win.” Press Association

Sports.title: 'Mischievous' Chris Sutton pokes fun at Match of the Day's 'dating' co-hosts Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates live on BBC radio
Sports.content:
BBC pundit Chris Sutton joked suggestively about his colleagues Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates on live radio, amid reports that the Match of the Day co-hosts are dating. Cates, 51, and Chapman, 52, have been stars of the BBC show's three-person presenter panel alongside Gabby Logan since the start of last season following Gary Lineker's departure. The pair have become public figures on our TV screens over recent years – but have grown close in private, with reports emerging on Sunday that the BBC stars have been dating. Chapman also serves as the regular host of BBC Radio 5Live's Monday Night Club, which typically wraps up the weekend's football. He was absent for the show on Monday night and Cates – an occasional stand-in host – also did not feature. Chapman's absence prompted regular guest Sutton to poke fun at the expense of the duo at the start of the show, after being introduced by stand-in presenter Alistair Bruce-Ball. Match of the Day co-hosts Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates are reportedly dating each other Cates and Chapman have been on the three-person presenter panel since Gary Lineker's exit Chris Sutton questioned the absence of host Chapman on the Monday Night Club live on radio amid the reports. Pictured: Sutton and Chapman on the show in 2025 'Chris Sutton has got a rather mischievous look on his face this evening, which worries me slightly,' Bruce-Ball said. Sutton responded: 'I just wondered where our leader is this evening, where's Mark?' with Bruce-Ball replying: 'Mark Chapman… Not here this evening.' 'So then normally second in charge is Kelly Cates... where's Kelly Cates this evening?' Sutton questioned. Bruce-Ball replied: 'I don't know Chris, otherwise engaged I think. If they are not listening to the show, whatever they are up to, it is available to listen by the podcast, if that is what they want to do.' Cates was instead hosting the Legends of Football awards, which saw Thierry Henry and Karen Carney honoured on the night. Chapman split with estate agent Clere Collier earlier this year, who accused him of starting the relationship with Cates while they were still together, an allegation he denies. Chapman and Cates became the main co-presenters for Match of the Day alongside Gabby Logan last season after Gary Lineker left. While their shifts presenting the show do not overlap, Chapman and Cates did appear on Celebrity Gogglebox on the same sofa together in July. Chapman, a highly respected broadcaster paid between £335,000 and £340,000 a year by the BBC, was already heavily involved with the show as Match of the Day 2 presenter before his promotion. Cates was hosting the Legends of Football awards, which honoured Thierry Henry and Karen Carney Clere Collier accused Chapman of starting the relationship with Cates while they were together, which he denies He was married to his wife Sara, the mother of their three children, for 19 years until she died aged 44 in 2020 after a battle with cancer. It was revealed in 2024 that he had started dating again after entering a relationship with estate agent and socialite Collier. They appeared to be in a good place, with Collier, who is based in Dubai, regularly making trips over to the UK to visit Chapman – and they were even pictured walking hand-in-hand through the streets of Altrincham together. She shared several gushing social media tributes towards Chapman, including one that labelled him as her 'one love' and 'devilishly handsome' after he turned 51, before they split in April this year. Meanwhile, Cates, daughter of Liverpool icon Sir Kenny Dalglish, was married to TV producer Tom Cates from 2007 until their divorce in 2021. The pair have two children together and lived in Chiswick in south-west London.

Sports.title: Dana White labels Eddie Hearn a NEPO BABY as war of words escalates between the promoters over Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua showdown
Sports.content:
Dana White's war of words with Eddie Hearn has taken another turn after the UFC and Zuffa Boxing chief essentially branded his rival a nepo baby.

The duo have been at each other's throats over various topics this year, from Conor Benn's future to the £150million blockbuster fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

Things have escalated over the last month. White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest and threatened crunch talks with broadcaster Netflix over White's attendance at Fury and Joshua's press conference on Wednesday in London.

And now, White has taken aim. He said on the Diary of a CEO podcast: 'Eddie's not the guy, Eddie's dad is the guy.

'And I'm not saying this to s*** on Eddie - I'm just being honest. I don't dislike Eddie. But he's not the guy; his dad's the guy.'

Dana White (left) has taken aim at Eddie Hearn (right) as their war of words continues - source: X - @danawhite

White branded Hearn a nep baby due to the sporting success of his father Barry (second left)

Barry Hearn, Eddie's father, has been a sports promoter since the 1970s and has had a huge influence on the likes of boxing, darts and snooker.

Eddie, though, now works in his own right though, according to White, is in his dad's shadow.

White continued: 'Frank Warren's the real guy. I just saw this interview with him; I was like, 'F***ing love it… all this f***ing talking and all this f***ing bulls***, let's f***ing fight.''

There had been doubt over whether the December 11 fight would in fact go ahead due to the involvement of White.

White, whose involvement has been criticised by sections of the British boxing public, was grilled by the media in a cagey press conference, where he labelled the bout a 's***show' while conceding he has 'no idea' if the contest will take place.

'I don't know. The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time,' he said. 'He hasn't done the fight any favours. I don't know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.'

When asked whether he would step aside to allow the fight to go ahead, White said: 'That's not up to me. I'm involved in the f***ing fight.

'If Eddie Hearn really cared about this f***ing fight — first of all the fight would've happened a f***ing long time ago, one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself.

'Listen, this whole thing's a s***show right now. We'll all know a lot more in the next three, four days, see how this thing plays out.'

The duo have been at a battle over who will promote the fight between Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua (right)

White had initially raised eyebrows when Benn left Hearn's Matchroom to join Zuffa.

It remains to be seen whether White will have any involvement.

Hearn said this weekend: 'At this point, (White's) completely cooked. What he actually said was, "We're doing the TV production". Which, again, in the contract, is prohibited.

'After that video (of White saying he was producing the fight), I spoke to Sela (the Saudi entertainment company listed as promoters of the event). I said, "Have you seen this video?" They said, in writing, "Yes, and it's completely untrue".

'(White) cannot do that under the contract. They want me to meet them in LA next week, which I probably will.'

Sports.title: Saudi Arabia to ABANDON their £2BILLION one-of-a-kind World Cup stadium plan to host football at 350 metres above ground level amid spiralling costs
Sports.content:
FIFA announced Saudi Arabia as the host nation for the 2034 World Cup almost two years ago but the organisers are already running into serious issues - with the construction of one of their biggest venues set to be scrapped.

Plans for one of the hosts' most ambitious venues for 2034, a futuristic elevated football stadium, have been scrapped, worrying fans and pouring £2billion down the drain in the process.

The NEOM stadium was sold as a one-of-a-kind sporting arena as a part of the 100-mile-long steel and glass structure known as The Line, a mirrored linear smart city meant to house nine million people, the original focal point of Saudi Arabia's NEOM mega project.

NEOM themselves own a Saudi Pro League Side, NEOM FC, that employ ex-Premier League stars such as Alexandre Lacazette, Said Benrahma and Malang Sarr.

NEOM was introduced nearly a decade ago as a key part of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030. The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for the country and under Vision 2030 Saudi Arabian investment in football over the last four years, via the wealth fund PIF, has been immense.

Eye-watering sums have been spent on in bringing in top players and coaches as well as building footballing infrastructure in preparation for the 2034 World Cup, with 15 stadiums in total being built or renovated.

Saudi Arabia have found success in some of their footballing investment but the NEOM stadium will be one to forget

Plans for a stadium in Neom saw a pitch 350m above ground and integrated into The Line

Plans for The Line, a 200 kilometre long row of skyscrapers, look set to be scaled back

The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts FIFA's new 48-team format and Riyadh have been working to transform 15 venues across five cities alongside dozens of training facilities.

MEED, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform, lists developments on the NEOM stadium as 'on hold' and the stadium has no listed completion date in their data. The remaining stadiums in the wider project are listed in various stages of development, with completion expected by 2033 at the latest.

But with plans for one of the most expensive and key venues seemingly shelved, questions will be raised over whether Saudi Arabia will be prepared come 2034.

Saudi Arabia also looks to be under increasing pressure from developments in the Iran war and has had to deal with heavy disruptions to critical infrastructure as well as energy shipments.

These issues will only add to Saudi Arabia's ever-growing costs and continue to hinder the Kingdom's efforts to prepare the nation for hosting the world's biggest sporting event in just under eight years time.

Sports.title: Grinning Cristiano Ronaldo returns to Al-Nassr training after walking out of Portugal camp - as Piers Morgan brands boss the 'Ten Hag of international football' by trying to 'belittle' star
Sports.content:
Grinning Cristiano Ronaldo returns to Al-Nassr training after walking out of Portugal camp - as Piers Morgan brands boss the 'Ten Hag of international football' by trying to 'belittle' star

A smiling Cristiano Ronaldo has returned to Al-Nassr training after stunningly walking out on the Portugal squad during the international break following a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus.

Al-Nassr warmly welcomed back the star, whose walkout dominated headlines around the Portugal camp during the international break.

'The GOAT in the heart of Najd, at Al Nassr', the Saudi Arabian club shared on social media, as Ronaldo arrived at the club's training centre.

While Ronaldo's focus has turned back to his club, his international future remains unclear after his clash with Jesus.

The star, 41, left Portugal's camp after Jesus's press conference last Wednesday, as the head coach appeared to confirm the forward would not start against Denmark in the Nations League.

It came after Ronaldo had been left on the bench for the entirety of the 2-1 win over Norway last weekend.

Cristiano Ronaldo returned to training with Al-Nassr after walking out of the Portugal squad during the international break

Ronaldo left the camp following a dispute with Portugal's head coach Jorge Jesus

Broadcaster Piers Morgan has claimed the dispute between Ronaldo and Jesus centres around broken promises by the Portugal boss, who he branded as the '[Erik] Ten Hag of international football'.

Ronaldo had previously spoken to Morgan in an explosive interview back in 2022, which effectively ended his Man United career, as he stated he did not respect then Red Devils boss Ten Hag.

Morgan, speaking on Sports Uncensored, has claimed Jesus tried to 'belittle and embarrass Ronaldo' and went back on his word over the star's playing time.

'What this goes down to is nothing about money or fame or any of these things,' Morgan said.

'He was given absolute guarantees about how he would be used, it was one of the reasons he decided to continue his international career.

'The new guy Jorge Jesus, who knows him from Saudi Arabia, said to him with the Nations League, they agreed he would play the first two games and would be rested for the next two.

'The first game he was told “you get 90 minutes” and he gets yanked after 67 minutes so he’s a bit p***ed off and afterwards the coach apologised to him and that he would go out and explain this shouldn’t have happened.

'He goes out and does the opposite, he pulls a Ten Hag, where he goes out and tries to belittle and embarrass Ronaldo and put him back in his box and say “all the players are as important to me”, which also p***es off Ronaldo.

Piers Morgan has claimed Jesus broke promises made to Ronaldo, leading to the star walking out of the camp

Morgan compared Jesus to former Man United boss Erik ten Hag, stating he had tried to 'belittle and humilate' Ronaldo

'Then he goes to Ronaldo and says “I know we said you would be rested for the second two games, but I want you for 30 minutes against Norway”.

'He went “okay, if that is what you want, I’ll do it”. He sits there and gets warmed up for 25 minutes and never gets on the pitch. So again he is p***ed off at the lack of respect.

'For him it is a question of respect, being promised one thing then the opposite happening, being warmed up and not used. Eventually he went f*** you and got on a plane and left.

'Does it sit well with you guys that Ronaldo might not get a farewell game for Portugal because a coach has decided he wants to be the big dog and humiliate him.'

Jesus has insisted Ronaldo could return in the next international break in November, saying: 'As far as I'm concerned, everything is open.

'It's up to Cris to decide his own life. In the next call-up, if Cris is playing and wants to be in the national team, why not?

'Resentment? Nothing, it was a misunderstanding. In my opinion, it's easy to resolve. When will I resolve it? I don't know. The game is over, and only afterwards will we know how things will turn out.

'It's not up to me. To reach an agreement with two people, both people need to talk and agree. That's not up to me.

Ronaldo's Portugal manager and team-mates insist he is welcome back should he choose

Jesus has insisted the situation is a 'misunderstanding' and is easy to resolve

'Just because it was him, and perhaps rightly so because he's a symbol, this whole problem of him coming on, warming up, not coming on. How many players warmed up today and didn't come on? Will there be a problem? No.

'With Cris it's different, he's a symbol. But is it a problem? For me it wasn't a problem. If Cris wants to and is playing for Al-Nassr, he'll be in the next squad. We talked before this squad and we can talk before the next one. It's Cris who will decide.'

The feud started when Ronaldo was left on the bench for Portugal's win over Norway – the first time in 18 years he had missed the full 90 minutes for the national side barring injuries and suspensions.

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

The tension seems to have boiled over following Jesus' press conference. The manager said: 'There was no incident whatsoever.

'Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

After leaving camp, Ronaldo said: 'I will tell the truth to all Portuguese people about the reasons that motivated my departure'

A sign has been placed outside the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, backing Ronaldo over Jesus

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.

'It's not difficult for me to focus,' he added. 'You know what's difficult for me? It's not understanding what's going on inside. It's not knowing how to train my players. That's what's difficult for me. The rest... zero.

'What's important is what we have to do. The things that happen don't separate the group, they haven't separated us and they won't separate us.'

Despite Ronaldo's walkout and controversy over his departure from the camp, Jesus's side won all four of the Nations League matches during the international break.

Ronaldo's former Man United team-mate Rio Ferdinand has insisted Jesus needs to apologise to the star and claims the Portuguese Football Association have been 'panicking' after the rift.

‘The coach needs to come out and apologise,' Ferdinand said on Rio Presents.

‘Trust me, I think he has to come out and say “listen I have judged this situation wrong”.

‘I am telling you, something has gone on, I am sure something has happened when you look between the lines.

Rio Ferdinand has claimed Jesus should 'come out and apologise' to Ronaldo

‘The president has come out and they’ve done the “Cristiano is the best, he’s the greatest, he’s this and that and the other".

‘They are trying to settle the situation, they are panicking behind the scenes now.

'This situation doesn’t play out the way it has if there are good communication skills.

'I think there has been terrible communication skills.

'I said this during the World Cup with Roberto Martinez and I think the same with this manager now, you have to sit with Cristiano Ronaldo and tell him this is what I want to do. And if you don’t want to be a part of it, then just tell me, but this is how I want it to work.

'That conversation I don’t believe has been had, because I don’t think you would be here with Cristiano going mid camp walking out like that.'

The international break had remarkably begun with Jesus and Ronaldo sat side-by-side at a press conference, where the former had labelled the star as a 'symbol of Portugal'.

Ronaldo had revealed he had considered retiring from international football in the summer before deciding to continue, but would walk away if the national team told him he was no longer required.

'Whenever they say they don't want me in the national team, I will be the first one to go,' Ronaldo said.

'When I think I am not adding anything to the team, or that I create an atmosphere, I will be the first to go. I will take my suitcase and leave.

'The Portuguese count on me, that's why I'm still here, just look at the numbers, I'm sure you can make some calculations, I'm still doing well.

'The day they don't count on me, no problem, I will leave. I will always be the No 1 fan of this federation.'

Sports.title: Luke Littler humbled at £15,000 youth tournament: World champion, 19, suffers surprise semi-final defeat after being told 'he can only lose'
Sports.content:
Luke Littler humbled at £15,000 youth tournament: World champion, 19, suffers surprise semi-final defeat after being told 'he can only lose'

Luke Littler has once again been knocked out of the World Youth Championship before the final – with his participation in the first place being questioned.

The 19-year-old is no stranger to the big stage, having won back to back senior world titles, picking up £1million for claiming victory last year in the process.

But, despite the world No1's widespread success on the biggest stage, he has taken it upon himself to still enter the Youth Championship as world champion twice in as many years.

Many thought he had little to gain and much to lose by entering, with defending champion and world No3 Gian van Veen opting not to take part this year.

It seemed a guarantee that Littler would win the title, but he fell short in the semi-finals for a second year in a row, losing 6-5 to Cam Crabtree, who will now go on to face Jan Schmidt in the final.

It comes a year after he lost to Beau Greaves in the semi-final last year – and he may yet enter in the future, with the tournament for those aged 16 to 24. Littler won the title in 2023.

Luke Littler was knocked out of the World Youth Championship at the semi-final stage for the second year in a row

The winner of the tournament will claim just £15,000 – significantly inferior money compared to what Littler is used to.

He won all three games in his group, then beat Lewis Cook, David Fidler, Archie Self and Harrison Leigh to reach the last four.

Some fans seemed to revel in his loss. One wrote on X: 'UNLUCKYYYYYYYY. Littler was never in a million years going to Minehead.'

Another posted: 'Luke Littler is officially washed and needs to retire!'

A third added: 'Hopefully this makes Luke Littler actually practice more, imagine if he practiced everyday how good he could be.'

Littler hit back after receiving stick last year, saying: 'It's the same venue as what we professionals play and obviously the likes of Gian van Veen - tour card holder, Keane Barry - tour card holder - both played, but I'm the one that gets it in the neck,'

'I didn't win, so a lot of people were happy, but I just thought I'd come and get used to playing first to five, first to six, and that's what I've done today and yesterday.'

After defeat on Monday, he took to Instagram to write: 'Nice day out today seen loads of old faces who I grew up playing youth darts with (JDC, England, Development Tour and many more).

'Fell short at the last hurdle fair play to Cam he's playing well atm overall a good day and some good practice put in.'

Wayne Mardle was one who questioned Littler's reason for playing in the competition

The defeat comes a matter of days after he lost against Luke Woodhouse in the opening round of the Grand Prix – and Sky Sports pundit Wayne Mardle has admitted Littler is off his game right now, as he questioned his reasoning for entering the Youth Championship.

'I don't know what he wants to gain from it,' Mardle said prior to the tournament. 'It doesn't make any sense to me.

'I just don't see the value time-wise. Because time-management's everything when you're playing a lot.'

He added after the defeat by Woodhouse: 'It's the fact that Luke Littler didn't play well. I just think he's underperforming right now, for whatever reason.

'Bearing in mind we're humans, we're not robots, we're not automatons, we do have off days as well. He's just having a couple of off days right now.'

The final will take place at the same time as the Players' Championship final at the end of November. Littler is almost certain not to qualify for that event after opting not to play in almost all of the qualifying events throughout the year.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel INCLUDED in Man United first-team photo - but doubt still surrounds future of the wantaway wonderkid as he turns 16 tomorrow, amid tug-of-war between Real Madrid and Barcelona
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel INCLUDED in Man United first-team photo - but doubt still surrounds future of the wantaway wonderkid as he turns 16 tomorrow, amid tug-of-war between Real Madrid and Barcelona

Wantaway Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has been included in Manchester United's squad photo of the season despite his desperate pleas to leave the club.

Gabriel shocked United last month when he made his intentions clear that he wanted to depart, despite the club's opinion that he would be much better off staying.

Barcelona and Real Madrid have been circling to try and sign the 15-year-old – who turns 16 on Tuesday – with the forward flying to the former to train.

It’s understood that he in fact travelled to Spain via France two weeks ago raising the possibility that his representatives may have spoken to Paris Saint-Germain as well. Bayern Munich are also known to have been tracking his progress.

But Madrid have been leading the chase for Gabriel and are believed to have held talks with his camp over the past few weeks.

He was included in United's official first team photo, which was released on Monday. It is understood the photo was taken last month on September 8, two days before he last played for the club.

JJ Gabriel (circled) has been included in Manchester United's first-team photo despite making his intention to leave known

He stood on the second row, next to veteran goalkeeper Tom Heaton and fellow youngster Harry Amass.

Daily Mail Sport understands that the Red Devils' stance has always been that they won’t de-register Gabriel and will continue to try to convince him that he is better off staying.

There is, though, acceptance within the club that the situation could change after his 16th birthday as the significance of an Irish passport kicks in – which allows players to bypass non European Union limits in foreign leagues and make international moves at a younger age easier.

Gabriel can also be legally represented by an agent at the age of 16.

The Old Trafford hierarchy are refusing to bow to Gabriel’s demand to rip up his registration and leave as a free agent – a move that could earn the club just £300,000 in compensation for a player who might soon be worth millions.

If United insist on keeping him until the end of the season, the 15-year-old could launch an appeal to the Premier League or even FIFA.

Because of his age, it would be difficult for United to stop his family from relocating to Spain or another European country, particularly if they can make a convincing argument it is being driven by a business opportunity unrelated to football and not because clubs are offering them a financial inducement.

FIFA regulations also include specific criteria over a young player’s education, but there are ways around those rules such as home-schooling.

Gabriel (pictured with Lamine Yamal in 2024) is of interest to the likes of Barcelona and Real Madrid in Spain

United insiders say the club’s main priority is Gabriel’s welfare, pointing out that the club still have a duty of care while he remains their player.

Barcelona gave Gabriel a tour of their club facilities in August 2024 when he was introduced to superstar Lamine Yamal who signed a shirt and posed for a photo. They are understood to have made their pitch to the player and are open to giving him time.

Gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football.

The youngster was set to sign a first-year scholarship at United at the age of 16 – which would have automatically triggered a lucrative professional contract on his 17th birthday.

United boss Michael Carrick said at his press conference before the international break that the youngster’s wellbeing remains paramount regardless of his future at Old Trafford.

‘I think I'd just repeat what I said the other day, really,’ said Carrick. ‘He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important that we certainly don't play anything out here. I think the exposure and the scrutiny and everything, you’ve got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything.

‘So the situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's okay is the important thing.’

Sports.title: 'There was no risk whatsoever': Thomas Tuchel defends England playing Alex Scott - with Bournemouth left frustrated as injured star faces up to two months on the sidelines
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has defended his decision to pick Alex Scott after the Bournemouth star was forced to withdraw from the England squad with a quad injury aggravated against Croatia. The 23-year-old Bournemouth midfielder made his first start for the Three Lions on Saturday night, having made his debut from the bench against Czech Republic days before. There are now fears that the Guernsey-born star could be sidelined for a couple of months, a blow for the Cherries who remain winless and 17th in the Premier League. Daily Mail Sport understands the club are frustrated at the development. He impressed for England, playing 70 minutes against Croatia, and Thomas Tuchel described him as playing at the 'highest level' - but he was said to be playing through pain from a pre-existing issue in order to represent his country. And on Monday, ahead of the Wembley clash with Czech Republic, Tuchel suggested that England did not take a risk playing him. ‘With Alex, it’s a strange one,' Tuchel said. ‘I’m very sad about it. Alex trained, both training sessions before the match full against Croatia. He did extra work after the training sessions. 'We knew he was in treatment but there were only green lights from himself, from the medics. When we were aware that there was a slight discomfort through the match, we asked him if he wants to come off. He said, “No”. 'After the match, he said, “Yeah, OK, it was the right thing to do, but I could have played 90 minutes, I don’t feel an injury”. Even the day after, here before we did the scan, he felt he was not injured. Alex Scott is withdrawing from the England international squad due to a quad injury Thomas Tuchel described Scott as 'the complete package' and at the 'highest level' 'It’s a strange one because it does not match the objectivity of the scan and the prediction of the time that he is obviously going to miss. It doesn’t match his feelings, and doesn’t match at all the process into the match and during the match.’ 'I can 100 per cent understand that Bournemouth is not happy and sad because they lose a key player,' Tuchel added. 'But I can just say from the moment we took the decision to let him play, there was absolutely no risk whatsoever apparent to me or our physical staff that we have a risk of an injury.' Tuchel says the England and Bournemouth medical departments have been involved in a 'totally open process' over Scott’s fitness and says club have to trust the national team. 'I’m not involved in discussions with clubs how to use them,” he added. 'I think the players are for two and a half weeks our players and, as much as we trust the clubs to put the players’ health first, I think the clubs have to trust us that we put the players’ health first. 'You can see it in our team selections and that will never change, but we are not on the phone to clubs asking for advice because then it would be an empty camp by now. 'It’s four matches for us and this is the most important thing. For these two-and-a-half weeks, these four matches matter more than anything else. It is an honour, a pride to play for your country. This is where the focus is.' Scott played on during the international break in honour of his grandfather, who died days before his debut and he described as one of his 'biggest fans'. 'I will always remember this place now. England debut - it's what dreams are made of,' Scott told BBC Radio 5 Live. 'Something that when I was younger, even 15 or 16, wasn't a reality at all so I've worked really hard and it's a proud moment for me and my family as well. 'My partner, she's been there with me for a good six years so she's seen everything, my parents are massive for me, my brother growing up [we were] playing football non stop, and my grandad passed away last week. 'For him, obviously it was a special thing and it's a shame that he didn't see it but he would have been looking down and proud of it. It was tough last week, I found out on camp just before the Spain game, he was the proudest man, he came to all my matches whenever he could and he was my biggest fan.' His withdrawal follows that of Nico O'Reilly, with the full-back returning to Manchester City after picking up a knock. Scott will return to Bournemouth for medical tests instead of potentially playing the Czechs again at Wembley on Tuesday. Scott is a key player for Bournemouth, who only sit 17th in the Premier League It robs him of his latest audition against Chelsea, where Bournemouth travel on Saturday. Xabi Alonso's club are interested in Scott. Chelsea bid for him at least once in the summer, though sources have claimed the Blues submitted three offers, up to £68million. Scott’s current contract with Bournemouth runs until 2028 and he has so far resisted signing a new deal despite the efforts of those inside the Vitality Stadium. Daily Mail Sport reported last week how Bournemouth sources have told those interested that they will only entertain negotiations for England’s newest international after they have established themselves in the Premier League once again this season. They are also not interested in selling this January. Bournemouth are currently 17th after five games, working under a new head coach in Marco Rose, and juggling Europe for the first time. While winless in the Premier League this term, they won 2-1 away at Real Sociedad in the Europa League, and beat Championship side Lincoln 4-0 in the Carabao Cup. As well as Chelsea, multiple other clubs enquired about Scott in the summer. That included Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester United and Manchester City, whose current crisis could deter transfer targets from joining, depending on what happens next in their case. If Bournemouth stand firm on not selling this January, Chelsea may be forced to look at bringing in an alternative midfielder, such as Monaco's Lamine Camara. His absence is a blow for Bournemouth, who are also missing striker Eli Junior Kroupi.
