Sports.title: FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay
Sports.content:
The FIA has given insight into why Formula 1 cars experienced technical issues ahead of Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The start of the Sepang race was delayed by 40 minutes due to a downpour; then a chaotic formation lap saw the likes front-row starters Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton suffer from a glitch which rendered throttle input ineffective, with numerous cars coming to a standstill. The red flag was waved.

The situation was branded “unacceptable” by Sergio Perez, who likened it to ‘being in a rental kart and running out of time’; Lando Norris described it “just horrible” and evidence that “we shouldn't have any of that stuff, the electronic side”, given this was linked to Formula 1’s new machinery, which features 47% electrical power.

FIA single-seater Nikolas Tombazis has now explained that, given F1 had never had competitive running in actual wet conditions this season, it was caught out by the power unit’s reaction to cars driving extremely slowly at that time. A software update therefore had to be carried out, hence a 53-minute delay to get the race restarted.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked, because there's been very little wet running this year, and there was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Basically, the formation lap, some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely. And that bug prevented the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Tombazis praised the FIA’s reaction when it came to fixing the issue as swiftly as possible.

“Once the problem happened, our guys realised very quickly what was happening and had to work under a lot of time pressure for an update to the software, which was issued to the teams, and the teams had to install it on their cars,” he added.

“So all of that took about 20 minutes. It may have felt like five hours for spectators waiting [for] a race and for everybody else, which is understandable, and we are sorry about that. But I think it was quite a fast reaction given the problem.”

Not everyone was so upset about some cars running into trouble, with eighth-placed Fernando Alonso joking at the end of an unusually good day for Aston Martin-Honda: “I had 50% DNFs this year, they never stopped the race for us.”

Sports.title: Russell: “You’ve got to laugh” at bad luck as F1 title drifts away
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell labelled his misfortune as laughable following Formula 1’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, where a power unit failure cost him a podium finish late on.

Russell was a lowly seventh on the grid at Sepang, but the correct choice of intermediate tyres on a damp track and a lightning getaway saw him surge to second into Turn 1, behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Russell was however passed by Max Verstappen as early as lap six, but the first safety car period gave him a chance to sweep past Antonelli around the outside of Turn 5 at the restart as the race leader dropped down to third – though the Italian youngster found a way back into second place just eight laps later.

Further drama did not disrupt the status quo in the top three, but a late safety car meant Russell had a chance to challenge his rivals for victory. However, the chance never came as a power unit failure took him out of the race before the final restart.

“You've almost got to laugh,” Russell told Sky Sports F1 after his third retirement this season – his second purely technical DNF. “It's beyond disappointment. It's just, so many times this season it's happened.

“Of course, it's a real shame, but… Just keep on fighting. Just keep on trying to go.

“The podium, of course, looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling and these questions, let's say.”

As he said, Russell will “keep on fighting”, but is equally aware of his deficit to championship rival Antonelli reaching an unprecedented 84 points.

The Briton steered clear of any sensational comments – he won’t say the title is out of reach – but his assessment is bleak nonetheless.

“I don't need to say I think it's gone or whatever,” he added. “But, of course, it’s exceptionally unlikely, and that's just the reality.

“I knew if I wanted to come back I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I've had luck not on my side. So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if the issue was on the other side, it would have been an 18-point gain.

“So, yeah, it's a real shame. It's a real shame, but that's just how it is.”

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the Bahrain GP in Malaysia had been one of his “worst experiences” personally, as Red Bull claimed its first victory of the year over the Silver Arrows and Russell suffered that setback.

“I'm so massively annoyed,” Wolff told Sky. “I'm not in a happy place.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“We didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will. Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us. We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.”

After praising Antonelli for ‘doing the job’, the Austrian added: “It's just this overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races. A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Perhaps Wolff was overdramatic there. At Sepang, Mercedes was outscored by Ferrari for just the first time since the summer break, and the Scuderia still is 151 points in arrears in the constructors’ championship. Meanwhile, Hamilton’s deficit to Antonelli in the drivers’ standings is up to 106 points.

Asked how to pull the team together after such a result, Wolff replied: “I think we have a good action plan. James [Allison, technical director] is really fully on top of it with his leadership team.

“That lifts my mood because I know we have such a tremendous group of people. In the same way as we have with HPP, they're going to sort it out. But that gives me real relief for the moment to know they are the best and they are going to find a solution. And I think we will come back strong.”

Sports.title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Verstappen wins chaotic race from Antonelli as Russell retires late on
Sports.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a disorderly Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, clinching his first victory of the season, as George Russell’s title hopes dwindled further with a late retirement.

After the race was delayed by an hour and a half due to dysfunctional software on a wet track, Verstappen outduelled both Mercedes to triumph as Russell was struck by a technical issue.

After a 40-minute delay due to a downpour, the formation lap began, with Isack Hadjar having a trip through the gravel as the whole field warmed up intermediate tyres. Several cars, including front-row starters Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, suffered software glitches that rendered throttle input ineffective. The red flag was waved, which delayed the race by a further 53 minutes.

When race finally got under way, only nine cars opted for intermediate tyres, including Verstappen, Kimi Antonelli, Russell and Hadjar. Others like Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri went for slicks, like Pierre Gasly, who spun out behind the safety car on lap one and dropped to 13th.

A standing start took place at the end of lap two, as Piastri, Gabriel Bortoleto, Lance Stroll, Nico Hulkenberg made late pitstops to switch from slicks to intermediates.

The Silver Arrows of Antonelli and Russell surged to the front of the pack easily at lights out, despite polesitter Verstappen having the same intermediates; the four-time world champion only narrowly held off Liam Lawson for third, with the Racing Bulls man enjoying a blistering getaway too.

Meanwhile, the Ferraris dropped down the order, along with Norris. Having clipped Nico Hulkenberg’s Audi, Leclerc pitted at the end of that lap and moved to intermediates, while team-mate Hamilton and his compatriot lost further dozens of seconds trying to make their gamble work – along with the Alpines, Oliver Bearman, Fernando Alonso and Valtteri Bottas.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Verstappen passed Russell for second place in Turn 4 on lap six, with the top three drivers within three seconds while fourth-placed Lawson was 10 seconds down; he was overtaken by Hadjar at the last corner on that same lap.

Verstappen caught Antonelli and started putting pressure on the race leader on lap eight; Antonelli went wide at the last corner but retained the lead.

Bottas-induced safety car levels the field

Bottas lost control in Turn 13 on lap nine and ended up benched in the gravel, causing a safety car period that was perfect timing for the inter-shod runners to switch to slicks, as the latter had become the quicker tyre compound, while allowing those who gambled on slicks to cut their losses.

Antonelli led from Verstappen, Russell, Hadjar, Lawson, Ocon, Lindblad, Sainz, Bortoleto and Piastri, with a variety of slick tyre compounds out on track – most interestingly the Mercedes drivers on mediums and the Red Bulls on softs – while Hamilton, Norris and Leclerc were down in 15th to 17th, with the Ferraris on softs and Norris on hards.

A ruthless Verstappen went around the outside of Antonelli at the restart in Turn 1, while Russell swept past in Turn 5, with the championship leader dropping to third in a few seconds. Meanwhile, Bortoleto and Sainz collided, with the Williams collapsing to 18th and the Audi driver handed a 10-second penalty.

As Verstappen pulled away from the Silver Arrows by over three seconds, Antonelli was getting impatient behind his team-mate, but team orders were not on the cards, so the Italian youngster found a way past in Turn 4 on lap 21. Further down the field, Hamilton was overtaking his opponents one after another, climbing to fifth by lap 22, while Leclerc broke into the top 10 on the following tour.

Antonelli went wide at the last corner and hit the pit entry bollard on lap 24, losing another two seconds to Verstappen, with the gap up to 7.5 seconds. He was now just one second ahead of Russell, but both gaps subsequently increased.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

The wave of second pitstops began on lap 29 for frontrunners, including Russell on lap 32, moving to softs – too early to his taste. Antonelli logically followed on the next tour to avoid being undercut, and so did Verstappen, now comfortably leading by 11 seconds.

Verstappen (briefly) cedes lead under VSC, Russell retires

As Hadjar found himself under pressure from Hamilton, the virtual safety car neutralised the race, with Alex Albon stopped due to a technical failure. Verstappen opted for a ‘cheap’ pitstop but ceded the lead to Antonelli; both Ferraris also changed tyres.

Mercedes eventually opted to pit both cars on the following tour, along with most frontrunners, until the VSC turned into a full safety car – which swayed the remaining ones.

Ahead of the final laps in green-flag conditions, Verstappen led Antonelli, Russell, Hadjar, Hamilton, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Lawson and Alonso, who fought his way into the top 10.

But before racing even got back under way, Russell stopped trackside with a technical issue and retired, while Norris was surprised by cars slowing down ahead and had a trip through the gravel and fell to 11th.

There were just four laps remaining when the safety car returned to the pitlane, and Verstappen mastered the restart; he never was at threat from Antonelli and triumphed. Hamilton found a way past Hadjar in Turn 1 on lap 53, clinching his first podium finish since Silverstone. The Frenchman also dropped behind the sister Ferrari of Leclerc.

Piastri finished sixth ahead of Lawson, while a combative Alonso held off Norris for eighth. Lindblad scored the last available point in 10th, underlining another strong day for Racing Bulls relative to the rival Alpine squad.

Having held sixth place early on, Esteban Ocon collapsed to 15th under the chequered flag, behind team-mate Bearman.

Sports.title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia descends into chaos as car trouble prompts red flag
Sports.content:
The Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia has been red-flagged after several cars suffered power unit gremlins during a wet set of formation laps.

After a heavy tropical thunderstorm, the action at Malaysian Sepang was set to get underway with a number of laps behind the safety car followed by a standing start.

But ahead of F1's first-ever wet event under the 2026 regulations, a number of cars suffered power unit gremlins in the rain, suspected to be software related.

Initially, polesitter Max Verstappen reported a lack of acceleration from his Red Bull before the Dutchman got going again. Soon after, second-placed Lewis Hamilton reported a similar issue on his Ferrari, with the Briton crawling around the first formation lap as the rest of the field passed him. One lap later, Hamilton too managed to get going again.

More cars, including Racing Bulls man Liam Lawson, Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, also appeared to struggle with similar problems, with race control suspending the start procedure and throwing a red flag.

With the grid mixed up as cars streamed into pitlane, race control will revert to the original grid positions when the running is resumed.

Race control eventually announced a start time of 16:33 local time, amounting to what would be a 50-minute delay.

Sports.title: Fan’s video shows moment software glitch slowed F1 cars to a crawl on formation lap | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s 2026 engine regulations faced fresh criticism yesterday following the farcical start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The race, which had already been delayed by rain, was postponed by almost an hour more after a software problem struck cars during the formation lap.

Pole-winner Max Verstappen and several drivers behind him slowed to a crawl as their power units would not allow them to accelerate. The cause was a software parameter set by the FIA, which required the governing body to apply new settings to the cars.

Verstappen said he had as much power as he did when the drivers raced in Lego cars in a promotional event.

“It was like the Lego race,” he said. “Same speed. It was insane, it’s the Lego power.

“At some point we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand what was going on. Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still.

“That’s not what you want, right, for the sport.”

The FIA said the cars’ loss of power was due to “an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration.”

Sports.title: Mercedes ‘don’t know if upgrade made us faster or slower’ – Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The long-awaited upgrade package Mercedes introduced last weekend may have made them less competitive, Andrea Kimi Antonelli has admitted.

Antonelli led the opening stages of yesterday’s race ahead of team mate George Russell . However both were overtaken by Max Verstappen , who went on to win the race.

Mercedes originally planned to introduce their new parts for the W17 at this weekend’s race in Singapore. They brought the upgrade forward after Formula 1 added last weekend’s round in Malaysia to replace the cancelled event in Bahrain.

However the unusually abrasive track surface at the Sepang International Circuit complicated the team’s efforts to understand the performance of its upgraded car. Antonelli qualified half a second slower than Verstappen.

He said the performance of the upgrade is “the question we need to answer because we don’t really know if it made us go faster or worse.”

However he pointed out the team has been less competitive at tracks which share some traits with Sepang. “It’s fair to say that this season, whenever we went on really old Tarmac, we’ve struggled. For example, in Zandvoort, McLaren was much quicker than us, especially on the older Tarmac.

“So I think maybe it’s just a fact that the Tarmac is very old and that for the tyres it’s very, very hard, and maybe we just struggle on this kind of Tarmac.

“But, of course, the track and the Tarmac made our life difficult in understanding whether it made us improve or not.”

The championship leader expects the team will have some answers before this weekend’s race. “I’m sure the team – they have a lot of data, especially after this weekend – and I’m sure for Singapore we will come with a much, much better view on the package and hopefully we can extract the full potential out of it.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: ‘Who decided these rules were best for F1?’ asks Sainz | Brief
Sports.content:
The farcical scenes during yesterday’s formation laps which delayed the start of the race by almost an hour prompted criticism from several drivers.

Grand Prix Drivers Association director Carlos Sainz Jnr was among those questioning why Formula 1 committed itself years ago to rules which have proved so problematic.

“[F1] needs to have a hard look at themselves and see how we ended up in this situation,” he said after the race. “It is clear the regs are extremely complicated for the drivers, for the teams, for the power units, for the manufacturers. It is too complicated.

“Again, my only question mark is who five years ago decided that this was the direction to go?”

F1 confirmed its current engine regulations in 2022, though the majority of the changes were substantially agreed before then. Mohammed Ben Sulayem became FIA president in December 2021.

Sainz’s father, multiple world rally champion Carlos Sainz, considered opposing Ben Sulayem in last year’s election, but chose not to. Ben Sulayem won re-election and subsequently moved to end presidency term limits, allowing him to serve as president as long as he likes.

Sports.title: Hamilton suspects he could have fought for win had he not started on slicks | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for victory at Sepang had he started on the right tyres.

The Ferrari driver qualified on the front row of the grid alongside Max Verstappen

“We were having a good weekend,” he said. “The car felt great in qualifying. It felt amazing to get to second.

“Me and my engineers were here ’til 11:30 last night just going over everything and I really, really felt today was the opportunity to have at least a good battle with Max.”

The original start was delayed due to rain. A further delay followed after a software problem caused several drivers, including Hamilton and Verstappen, to slow to a crawl during the formation lap.

“My power didn’t come back and I had to stop on-track and restart the car and then we all ended up in the pit lane,” said Hamilton. “Thankfully, we all got back to our positions.”

By the time race control were ready to start the race, the track had dried considerably, though it was still damp. Hamilton and his team chose to start the race on slick tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“There was such a long wait and we were debating what tyre to go on to. And I said, ‘look, there was a lot of spray on the laps to the grid.’

“I went into the pit lane, I looked at the ground, I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ I went to the pit wall and I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ And they’re like, ‘Yeah, but because it’s been so long, it’s definitely going to dry up real quick and maybe we’re already in the crossover.’

“So, anyway, as a team we ended up taking that soft and when we were at the end of the pit lane and these two took off their blankets and they were on inters [I knew] we were in trouble.”

The track took a long time to dry and those who opted for intermediates gained a significant advantage at the start. Hamilton urged the team not to bring him into the pits for another change.

“As everyone had overtaken me, they’re like, ‘we stop.’ [But] I know we’ve already [lost] another 26 seconds, what’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I [said] ‘let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.’ And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people.”

Hamilton began to make progress on his softs once the Safety Car came out and he was back within range of other cars.

“The car felt great then after that. Really good pit stops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy.

“For us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. But, of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.”

He said he will have an “open dialogue” with the team about the decision to start the race on slicks.

“We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that.

“So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which was the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting. I thought today, as I said, was a chance for us potentially to try and fight Max for the win, but maybe we can do that next week.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 must learn lessons from formation lap shambles at Sepang – Hamilton | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen were unimpressed with the delay to the start of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The pair urged Formula 1 to learn lessons from the software problem which struck both their cars during the original formation lap. Both drivers and several of their rivals slowed to a crawl, leading F1 to abandon the attempt to start the race.

“It was insane,” said Verstappen. “At some point we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand what was going on.

“Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still, and I saw [Hamilton] crawling.”

“That’s not what you want, right, for the sport,” he added.

Hamilton’s Ferrari came to a complete stop. “I had to stop on track and stop the car and engine and restart it,” he said. “I’ve never done that before.”

“I hope there is a lesson learned,” he added.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Race control summoned the field into the pits and distributed revised software parameters to all the teams in order to address the problem. The problem added almost an hour to the original delay, caused by rain.

“They had to update the software and then you have to load it into the car,” said Hamilton. “I guess some had some faster laptops than others.”

The FIA confirmed it “removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release” to address the problem.

“It was just like driving at 35 kilometres, going uphill, actually losing speed,” Verstappen explained. “I don’t know exactly, because when you go too low in speed and too low RPM, for whatever reason, then it just bogs down, and normally it takes one or two seconds and it comes back.

“That’s basically also what I had in the start. But somehow that didn’t trigger in the first software round, and then in the second software round it was a bit better, luckily.”

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Lacks Substance For Bivol, Warren Argues
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s title opportunity has come before his stamina has caught up, according to Frank Warren, who told Playbook Boxing that a Dmitry Bivol fight would be a severe mismatch.

His victory over Conor Wallace leaves Matchroom with an awkward choice. Pursuing Bivol now risks exposing Whittaker before he can correct his weaknesses. Taking a demanding preparation fight risks losing the opportunity through defeat.

“He runs out of gas. He hasn’t got a great engine,” Warren said to Playbook Boxing. Asked about facing Bivol, he added: “Anyone who makes that fight should be reported to the NSPCC.” “Matchroom done a good job in promoting him. He got everybody talking about him, but you’ve got to have some substance then. And the substance at the end of the day just isn’t there.”

Wallace’s late rally supplies the strongest evidence for Warren’s criticism. Whittaker struggled when his opponent kept advancing and forced him to work while tired. Bivol’s disciplined combinations and positioning could make those demands arrive earlier, with fewer opportunities to recover.

Waiting alone will not solve that. Whittaker needs rounds that teach him to control his effort, maintain his defense, and respond when an opponent refuses to cooperate. An easy stoppage would offer little evidence that he has learned those lessons.

Warren’s suggestions of Joshua Buatsi or Willie Hutchinson come with an obvious commercial incentive: either could give Queensberry a valuable victory over a heavily promoted Matchroom fighter. They would also test whether Whittaker can withstand sustained pressure from a dangerous domestic contender.

That is the difficulty with using either as preparation. The test could become the defeat that derails the Bivol route.

Whittaker’s highlights have accelerated his popularity. His ring education needs more time. Once fatigue reduces his movement, the defensive habits behind the spectacle become harder to conceal.

Matchroom must now decide how much risk to accept while bringing his boxing up to the level his promotion already promises.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Dismisses Ermal Hadribeaj’s Knockout Threat
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora sees little behind Ermal Hadribeaj’s knockout predictions, telling The Ring that his unbeaten mandatory challenger presents no threat in power or boxing ability ahead of their October 17 fight in Las Vegas.

Hadribeaj has eight knockouts in a 23-0-1 record, which makes stopping the WBC light middleweight champion an ambitious promise. His best victory, a unanimous decision over Bakary Samake in May, earned him this opportunity without showing that he possesses the punch to finish Fundora.

“Boxing-wise, IQ-wise or anything, I don’t see no threat at all,” Fundora told The Ring. “Punching power? No, there’s not really anything in my mindset that is realistic in that situation.”

Fundora’s confidence is understandable. Hadribeaj hasn’t beaten anyone with the champion’s combination of height, output, and experience. Getting past Samake in an eliminator was a useful win, but dealing with a 6-foot-6 southpaw who can maintain pressure through repeated exchanges requires considerably more.

The challenger’s unbeaten record offers no answer to how he will react when Fundora forces him to work harder than he has against previous opposition. If Hadribeaj cannot discourage him with his punches, finding enough room to box could become difficult.

Still, Fundora has already experienced the danger of giving an opponent opportunities to land. Brian Mendoza knocked him out in the seventh round in April 2023. That defeat should remain a reason to stay defensively responsible, even against someone whose record suggests modest power.

A low knockout total doesn’t prevent a challenger from landing one damaging shot. Fundora’s willingness to fight at close range can give opponents chances they would struggle to create if he consistently used his reach.

Fundora has won four straight since the Mendoza loss, most recently stopping Keith Thurman in six rounds. Hadribeaj represents another chance to build toward bigger fights, including a possible unification with Jaron Ennis.

The challenger has earned his title shot. His knockout prediction requires evidence he has yet to provide.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Questions Anthony Joshua’s Chin Against Tyson Fury
Sports.content:
Frank Warren believes Anthony Joshua’s physique will offer little protection against Tyson Fury, saying that punch resistance and stamina favor his fighter in their heavyweight showdown.

“One thing you can’t do, you can’t put muscles on chins,” Warren said to Playbook Boxing. His argument is that Fury has recovered from heavy punishment, while Joshua’s defeats against Andy Ruiz Jr. and Daniel Dubois exposed weaknesses that strength and conditioning cannot solve.

Warren pointed to the punchers who have put Fury down, particularly Deontay Wilder, and emphasized his ability to recover. He also claimed Fury has “much more stamina than AJ.”

Joshua’s muscular build has never prevented him from being hurt. The more relevant question is what happens afterward. Against Ruiz and Dubois, he struggled to regain control once the damage was done. Fury has repeatedly survived knockdowns and found a way back into fights, giving Warren a reasonable basis for that comparison.

However, those recoveries came at a cost. Fury’s ability to survive Wilder’s punches does not guarantee he can absorb Joshua’s at this stage of his career. Warren himself described both heavyweights as being in the “late autumn” of their careers, which makes their current condition more relevant than their strongest performances years ago.

Joshua also does not need to match Fury’s endurance if he can land cleanly before the fight develops into a prolonged contest. His opportunity is to punish openings without rushing his work or leaving himself exposed to the return.

Warren acknowledged that both men can punch and argued that their willingness to commit under fire could decide the outcome. That brings his criticism back to something more specific than muscles: whether Joshua can remain effective after taking a damaging shot.

Fury’s history gives Warren confidence in that situation. Joshua’s history gives him a target to attack. Neither establishes how much punishment either heavyweight can still withstand.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Keeps Ben Davison For January Return
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma will return in January with Ben Davison still training him, Frank Warren confirmed to Playbook Boxing following a team meeting to discuss his defeat against Filip Hrgovic.

Warren identified Itauma’s pursuit of a knockout as the mistake that exhausted him. Keeping Davison means their next camp must produce a more controlled approach, with Itauma learning to win rounds without trying to finish his opponent with every punch.

“He’s staying with Ben and the team,” Warren said to Playbook Boxing. “You’ve got to judge him now on his results, which is what we’ll do.”

Warren said Itauma and his team met at the Queensberry offices on Friday, giving everyone time to review the defeat before discussing changes. He did not name a January opponent.

The promoter believes Itauma’s power would have stopped most heavyweights that night, claiming “98%” would not have survived. Hrgovic did, and that exposed the danger of building a fight around an early finish. Once the knockout failed to arrive, Itauma had spent energy he needed for the later rounds.

Warren described a fighter who needed to return to his jab, move, and take an easier round. Those are practical adjustments, but Itauma must be willing to make them while an opponent is still in front of him. Having the tools in training is different from choosing to use them under pressure.

A January victory would get Itauma moving again. The more useful evidence will be how he achieves it. Another quick stoppage could leave the questions from the Hrgovic defeat unanswered, especially if the opponent offers little resistance.

Davison’s continued involvement gives the partnership an opportunity to demonstrate that it can correct the pacing issue. Warren praised Itauma’s heart and believes he can challenge for another world title fairly soon, but that ambition depends on developing an approach that works when his power cannot settle the fight early.

Sports.title: John Fury Refuses to Attend Tyson Fury’s Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
John Fury is refusing to attend Tyson Fury’s fight with Anthony Joshua, claiming he cannot stomach the figures running the show and refuses to hang around without an official role. Rather than watching the broadcast live, the patriarch plans to wait by the phone for the final result.

“I’ll be honest with you, no. No, I won’t be attending,” John told Playbook Boxing. “Let me tell you, you have more chance of seeing a cow fly than me bothering with it.”

This goes beyond dodging the media crush. John refuses to sit ringside as an ordinary ticket holder while outside handlers run Tyson’s corner.

“I don’t like the people in it, and I know accidents can happen. I’m not involved, so I don’t want to go to the fight,” he continued. “I don’t need validation to go to a boxing match and sit there and be an absolute spare p**** at the wedding.”

His admission of having no official capacity tells the entire story. John ties his presence directly to authority; stripped of control, he sees zero value in showing up. His wedding analogy makes that crystal clear, signaling that he refuses to occupy a seat unless he is dictating terms.

Being a father in the arena carries plenty of meaning on its own.

Backing his boy should not depend on calling the shots in training, barking orders from the corner, or liking every promoter and trainer in the building. John makes it clear that bruised pride over camp authority is enough to keep him home on fight night.

Tyson holds total authority to assemble whatever team he trusts to handle fight preparation and ring instructions. John griping from the sidelines does not make those camp decisions flawed. The quality of Tyson’s camp will show under the lights, regardless of his father feeling frozen out.

His cryptic comment about accidents provides zero proof that the organizers issued an actual ban, leaving the drama strictly self-generated.

“I’ll be doing what his mother does,” John added. “I’ll wait for somebody to tell me who wins the fight.”

Shutting off the live broadcast turns his absence into a total boycott. John would rather wait for a delayed phone call than watch his son trade punches, putting his personal grudge ahead of the actual event. His protest is obvious, proving that without an active role on the headset or in the corner, he simply has no stomach to tune in.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Dismisses Keyshawn Davis and Richardson Hitchins
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is giving Keyshawn Davis and Richardson Hitchins little reason to expect a fight, dismissing their name recognition rather than discussing what either offers inside the ring. Both need a win that builds demand, because calling Ryan out gives him little financial incentive to face them.

“Who the f*** knows them?!” Ryan said to FightHype about Keyshawn Davis and Richardson Hitchins.

Ryan’s point is that neither has built much recognition among casual boxing fans. Their lack of fights against notable opponents has limited their exposure, leaving them asking for a lucrative fight without bringing a large audience of their own.

The commercial argument has some logic. A dangerous opponent who brings a limited audience can demand considerable preparation without generating the revenue of a more recognizable name. From Ryan’s perspective, taking that risk becomes less attractive when other opponents offer a larger event.

However, name recognition does not measure how competitive a fight would be. Keyshawn’s combination punching and Hitchins’ patient boxing present different challenges. Dismissing their drawing power leaves those sporting questions unanswered. Ryan could have a sound business reason to prefer another opponent while still passing over a demanding fight.

Beating a star is one of the quickest ways for a fighter to become known. Ryan’s argument leaves Keyshawn and Hitchins needing that kind of opportunity while their lack of popularity gives him a reason to refuse it. They could keep winning and still struggle to attract the audience he wants an opponent to bring.

Fighting each other would give Keyshawn and Hitchins a chance to strengthen their case. The winner would have a significant victory to offer, although the performance would help determine how much interest it generated. A cautious points win could add to his record without making a Ryan fight much easier to sell.

Keyshawn and Hitchins need a victory that makes people want to see them fight Ryan. Another callout is unlikely to change his thinking. Until either builds that demand, Ryan has a convenient business argument for passing over an opponent who could be difficult to beat.

Sports.title: Frank Smith Backs Odel Kamara To Reach Top
Sports.content:
Frank Smith believes Odel Kamara can reach the top of boxing, but the 22-year-old’s debut against Thodoris Ritzakis offered reasons to question that projection. His punching technique and apparent physical limitations make the leading fighters at 154 look a long way beyond him.

“He can go to the very top of the sport,” Smith told talkSPORT. “He’s just 22 years old. And I think what we’re seeing now is a lot of fighters turning over a lot younger in their careers, not staying in the amateurs for too long. And I think that happened too often, maybe over the last sort of 10, 15 years or so.”

Kamara halted Ritzakis on Saturday night, but his habit of loading up from the bleachers creates massive defensive red flags. He threw his entire upper body into every delivery to manufacture power, lunging forward with wide arcs. That reckless aggression from Kamara overwhelmed the novice, Ritzakis, but a skilled counterpuncher would simply time the looping shots, slip inside, and tag his exposed chin before his feet ever reset.

The excessive labor behind Kamara’s offense remains a glaring problem. Natural punchers generate concussive force through tight, compact mechanics and sudden snap. Kamara strains for leverage, hurling himself into right hands and leaving himself defenseless whenever an opponent smothers his extension or makes him miss clean.

That wild output also threatens his gas tank. Emptying the tank on maximum effort haymakers drains stamina fast, and a brief early stoppage proves nothing about his engine under deep waters. Solid opposition will make Kamara fight in retreat, forcing him to expend energy on defense while desperately trying to detonate those same wide swings.

Pitting Kamara against the elite at 154 pounds exposes the promotional spin for what it is. Jaron Ennis, Vergil Ortiz Jr., and Sebastian Fundora possess lethal finishing ability, relentless punch output, and seasoned ring intelligence. Kamara showed zero traits suggesting he belongs anywhere near that bracket. He lacks a true junior middleweight frame, his power requires a massive windup instead of sudden leverage, and his wild output guarantees his gas tank empties early against durable operators.

Time remains on Kamara’s side at 22, but protective matchmaking can only mask mechanical flaws for so long. Matchroom could orchestrate an undefeated run against handpicked domestic opposition and eventually steer him into an alphabet title shot against a paper champion.

Collecting a vacant strap will never fool sharp eyes into believing Kamara reached elite status. Frank Smith is selling dreams, but Kamara’s debut provided zero proof that he can compete at the highest level.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Talks Legacy Before Finishing Wardley Business
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois expects a smoother win over Fabio Wardley on October 17, but his talk of becoming a heavyweight legend runs ahead of what he has established. Wardley dropped him twice in their first fight, giving the challenger good reason to believe the rematch can end differently.

“Even better and even smoother than last time,” Dubois told Queensberry. “I feel like I’ve improved and, having been the champion, I’ve improved double. That’s some boxing history I’ve got—a two-time world champion—and now I need to go down as a legend.”

Dubois earned credit for recovering to stop Wardley in the 11th round in May. That showed toughness, stamina, and the power to turn a dangerous fight around. It also showed that Wardley can put him on the floor. Claiming substantial improvement is easy; showing how he will prevent Fabio from landing those damaging punches is the test.

The wins over Jarrell Miller and Filip Hrgovic required Dubois to work through difficult stretches, too. Joe Joyce stopped him, and Oleksandr Usyk beat him twice inside the distance. Those results do not erase his achievements, but they give little support to the idea that beating Wardley once makes the return fight straightforward.

His knockout of Anthony Joshua remains his biggest-name victory. Still, Joshua’s vulnerability to heavy punches limits how much that performance tells us about Dubois against the other leading heavyweights. Flattening Joshua did not translate into solving Usyk.

Dubois has a decent chin, but shots he does not see coming can hurt him. Wardley already knows he has the power to exploit that vulnerability, and he does not need to win every round to threaten the champion. Dubois needs to beat Wardley again, then pursue the other champions.

Unification victories and successful defenses would build the record behind his ambition. Right now, he is discussing his place in heavyweight history while preparing to face a man who nearly ended his latest title run before it began.

Ghana News.title: Nigerian military aircraft crashes, killing 32
Ghana News.content:
A Nigerian ​military plane flying from Benin City ‌to Lagos crashed on Monday in southwestern Ondo state, killing 25 passengers and seven crew ​members.

President Bola Tinubu, confirming that ​there were no survivors, expressed "profound sadness" and ⁠extended condolences to the families of ​those aboard.

"The Chief of Air Staff has ​briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation ​into the cause of the crash ​to prevent future occurrences," Tinubu said in a ‌statement.

The ⁠Air Force ATR-42 aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos when air traffic controllers lost contact ​with it ​at 0813 ⁠GMT on Monday, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said. The accident was one ​of the deadliest air disasters ​in ⁠Nigeria in recent years.

The wreckage was later located near the coastal town of Igbokoda, ⁠where ​search and rescue teams ​were deployed.

Ghana News.title: MTN encourages Ghanaians to use MoMo for saving, investing and financial planning
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana is encouraging customers to move beyond basic Mobile Money transactions and take advantage of the wider range of digital financial services available on the MoMo App.

The telecommunications company says the initiative forms part of efforts to deepen digital financial inclusion and help customers use technology not only to transfer money, but also to save, invest, access credit and plan for their financial future.

Speaking during MomoFest, Manager for Brands and Communication at MTN Ghana, Isaac Agyenim Boateng, said the company was repositioning MoMo from a transaction platform to a broader financial-wellness tool.

“For us as a business now, we are moving from wallet to financial well-being,” he said.

Mr Boateng noted that although many customers continue to rely on the *170# short code for basic transactions, the MoMo App provides access to a wider range of financial services.

These include savings, investments, loans and pension products, giving customers more opportunities to manage and grow their finances through their mobile devices.

Taking MoMo to customers

MTN has, over the past two weeks, intensified its engagement with customers across the Volta Region, including Ho and surrounding communities.

According to Mr Boateng, teams have been visiting communities, homes and offices to help customers download the MoMo App and understand how to use its various services.

He said the campaign was not simply about encouraging more people to download the application, but also about changing how customers use digital financial services.

The objective, he said, was to help customers move from simply sending and receiving money to using their digital wallets to build greater financial stability.

Security remains critical

Mr Boateng also urged customers to remain vigilant against fraud, assuring them that the MoMo platform has security measures in place.

He said MTN’s security systems were complemented by continuous customer education through SMS messages, social media campaigns, weekly fraud-prevention tips and educational content on its YouTube channels.

He, however, cautioned customers never to disclose their MoMo PINs or one-time passwords.

“Your PIN is your key. It is a key to your wallet,” he warned.

Cashless payments transforming businesses

Some vendors participating in the MomoFest activities also highlighted the growing importance of cashless payments to their businesses.

Vendor Abandoned Grace Oma Mefut said digital payments had reduced the risks associated with carrying large amounts of cash after making sales.

For Millicent, popularly known as MG of MG Scoreset, cashless transactions have become an important part of her online business, providing customers with a convenient way to make payments.

She said the growing adoption of digital payments was changing how businesses operate and interact with customers.

MTN Ghana says the expansion of digital financial services could make financial services more accessible while encouraging customers to move from simply using money digitally to managing their financial lives digitally.

Ghana News.title: Absa Bank Ghana names Stephen Ato Frimpong as Board Chair
Ghana News.content:
Absa Bank Ghana Limited has appointed Stephen Ato Frimpong as its Board Chair, effective October 1, 2026.

Mr Frimpong joined the board as an Independent Non-Executive Director on March 1, 2021.

During his tenure, he has chaired the Board Audit Committee and the Board Social, Sustainability and Ethics Committee, and previously chaired the Board Risk Committee.

He has also served on the Board Remuneration Committee and the Board Information Technology, Cybersecurity and Payment Systems Committee.

Mr Frimpong brings extensive experience in corporate governance, audit, finance, business operations, risk management, compliance, ethics, fraud investigations, information technology, cybersecurity and data privacy.

Before retiring in 2020, he served as Vice President and Chief Audit Executive at Kimberly-Clark Corporation in the United States, where he led the company's global internal audit function, including support for its compliance programmes and ethics-related investigations.

Mr Frimpong holds a Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of Cape Coast and a Master of Accounting degree from the University of Texas at Austin in the United States.

He is a Certified Public Accountant and Certified Management Accountant.

He succeeds Mrs Frances Adu-Mante, who concluded her tenure as Board Chair on September 30, 2026.

Mrs Adu-Mante joined the board as an Independent Non-Executive Director in September 2017 and was appointed Board Chair in January 2020.

Absa Bank Ghana expressed its appreciation to Mrs Adu-Mante for her leadership, service and contribution to the bank.

The board, management and staff also congratulated Mr Frimpong on his appointment and expressed confidence in his leadership as the bank enters its next phase of growth.

Ghana News.title: Pickford ‘almost caused crash’ with careless driving
Ghana News.content:
England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford

England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford nearly caused a crash with two other cars during a bout of careless driving in his £200,000 Lamborghini supercar, a court has heard.

The 32-year-old was pulled over by police after ignoring a give-way sign, forcing two cars to slam on their brakes, and then speeding off into the distance.

The incident occurred in the Cheshire town of Knutsford on 14 April, leading to a criminal prosecution for driving without due care or attention.

Pickford, who has 336 appearances for Everton and 92 England caps, has pleaded guilty to the charge and will next appear at Chester Magistrates' Court on 7 December.

According to court documents, PC Cecil Ricardo of Cheshire Police said he had just left the station when he saw Pickford's blue Lamborghini Urus with personalised number plates.

"I was stationary on Bexton Road, Knutsford, waiting for traffic signals to turn green," he wrote.

"I then witnessed a blue Lamborghini Urus driving along Princess Street.

"It reached the junction with Toft Road, completely ignored the give way lines and pulled onto Toft Road causing two vehicles to slam on their brakes to avoid a collision.

"The Lamborghini then sped down Toft Road, Knutsford."

'Completely ignored'

Ricardo said he activated his lights and siren to set off in pursuit of the Lamborghini, noticing he was driving at 50mph (80.4 kmh) while the Lamborghini "was still pulling away".

"The speed limit on that stretch of Toft Road, Knutsford, is 30mph," he noted.

The officer said Pickford appeared to notice the police car giving chase and pulled over.

Pickford pleaded guilty in writing and told Warrington Magistrates Court: "I would like to attend court to put forward my mitigation."

His case was formally adjourned last week.

Pickford, who started his career at Sunderland before loan spells at six clubs including Burton Albion, Bradford City and Preston North End, has featured for England at the 2018, 2022 and 2026 World Cups, and was in goal for the country's Euro 2020 and 2024 final appearances.

Ghana News.title: Author and former politician Jeffrey Archer dies aged 86
Ghana News.content:
Jeffrey Archer says he has written his final book

Bestselling author and former politician Jeffrey Archer has died at the age of 86.

Archer sold more than 300 million books in his five-decade writing career, including the Clifton Chronicles and Kane and Abel, and often set his novels in his hometown of Wellington, Somerset.

In a statement, Archer's publisher HarperCollins said the author died "suddenly and peacefully at home" on Monday between writing sessions.

The former Conservative MP was jailed for perjury in 2001 after being found guilty of lying and cheating in his 1987 libel case against the Daily Star.

Archer was born in north London on 15 April 1940 but would quickly move to Weston-super-Mare in Somerset, where his family bought a house from John Cleese's mother.

In 1969, Archer was elected MP for the Lincolnshire constituency of Louth.

He served as an MP for five years before becoming Conservative Party chairman.

His political career was paused in 2001 when he was jailed for four years for perjury and perverting the course of justice.

He was found to have lied in libel action he had brought against The Star newspaper, in which he was awarded £500,000 in damages.

He was released in 2003 and returned to the House of Lords until he retired in 2024.

His last book, Adam and Eve, is set to be released this week, HarperCollins added, describing him as a "master storyteller" whose readers "meant everything to him".

Last week, Archer returned to his former school to promote his last book.

"It's wonderful to come back. What I got a real thrill about when I was walking towards the library is seeing the young boys and girls and thinking, 'that's the next generation'," Archer said at Wellington School.

Archer was due to attend the Cheltenham Festival on Saturday to discuss final his novel.

He and his wife Mary had celebrated their 60th wedding anniversary this year, HarperCollins said.

The pair have two sons and five grandchildren.

Jeffrey Archer, pictured here with Margaret Thatcher, served as a Conservative MP and party chairman

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described Archer's death as a "huge shock".

Writing on X, she said: "I am incredibly saddened to hear this news. He had sent me a lovely message just this morning and was always a great source of encouragement to me personally."

Paying tribute to the bestselling author, Kate Elton, HarperCollins UK CEO and Jeffrey's editor, said: "It has been one of the great privileges of my publishing life to have been Jeffrey Archer's editor.

"He was the master storyteller and an editor's dream - phenomenally hard-working, utterly committed to completing draft after draft to get every word as perfect as possible, and a true champion of the 'team' nature of great publishing."

HarperCollins said the author had been at the Leicester Square Theatre in London on Sunday, signing books for fans with broadcaster Gyles Brandreth.

Writing on X, Brandreth said: "Just yesterday I did a show with Jeffrey Archer to celebrate his new novel – he said it was to be his last.

"He was in the most wonderful, ebullient form and had such a great reception from a packed house. He was funny, engaging and self-deprecating – a great storyteller to the last."

Former Conservative chancellor Nadhim Zahawi paid tribute to the bestselling author on X, describing him as a "dear friend and extraordinary human being".

He wrote: "His gift for storytelling was matched by his wit, warmth and boundless energy. Life was never dull in Jeffrey's company."

Ghana News.title: No education reform can succeed without teachers – Education Ministry
Ghana News.content:
The Education Ministry has reaffirmed the critical role of teachers in Ghana’s education system, saying no meaningful education reform can succeed without their active involvement.

The Ministry made the statement as Ghana joins the rest of the world to celebrate World Teachers’ Day 2026.

In a message marking the occasion, the Ministry congratulated and commended teachers across the country for their dedication, professionalism and sacrifice in shaping the minds and futures of Ghanaian children.

It particularly recognised teachers working in deprived and hard-to-reach communities.

The Ministry said the government’s education transformation agenda goes beyond expanding access to education.

It said the focus is also on improving the quality of education, learning outcomes, relevant skills and human capital development.

“We recognise that no education reform can succeed without teachers,” the Ministry said.

It added that it would continue working with teachers, their unions and other stakeholders to strengthen the teaching profession.

The Ministry said this would include efforts to support professional development and address issues affecting teachers’ welfare and working conditions.

It also called on parents, communities, and the wider public to appreciate and support teachers for their contributions to Ghana’s development.

The Ministry said teachers remain “at the heart of Ghana’s education system” and play a critical role in preparing the next generation.

“To every teacher, we say:

“Thank you for your dedication. Thank you for your sacrifice. Thank you for shaping Ghana’s future.”

The Ministry ended its message by wishing teachers across the country a happy World Teachers’ Day.

Ghana News.title: Gauff condemns racist abuse after China Open win
Ghana News.content:
Coco Gauff says she suffered racial abuse on social media following an incident in her win over 16-year-old Sun Xinran at the China Open.

The American had been serving at 4-5 in the first set when her Chinese opponent thought she had hit a winner.

However, Gauff raised her hand to stop play due to a flickering light in the side panels surrounding the court.

Gauff won the next three points to hold for 5-5 before she closed out the set, and then dropped just one game in the remainder of the contest as she claimed a 7-5, 6-1 victory to reach the last 16 in Beijing.

The world number four gave a lengthy explanation of why she stopped the point in a post on X and said it was "an unfortunate situation" but "out of my control", adding that Sun had understood and accepted her apology.

Gauff then responded to a reply to her original post which included racist language.

"You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff wrote.

"The amount of racist comments/direct messages I've received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief."

Gauff is far from the first player in the women's game to suffer social media abuse.

A report in July said female players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025.

The WTA and World Tennis said "collective action" was required to make "significant progress" in tackling abuse.

Ghana News.title: Medvedev disqualified for hitting spectator with ball
Ghana News.content:
Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from the China Open after hitting a spectator in the face with a ball during his semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Third seed Medvedev trailed Djokovic 7-5 5-3 when the Serb hit a winner beyond him for 15-15.

The ball ricocheted off the back of the court and Medvedev swiped at a backhand in annoyance, sending the ball into the air and hitting a spectator who was sitting in the front row of the stand behind him.

The fan doubled over holding his face and was still holding his eye as he was helped out of the arena.

After speaking with umpire Mohamed Lahyani and an ATP official, Russia's Medvedev approached the net to shake hands with Djokovic.

"Terribly sorry to the spectator, first of all," Medvedev said.

"I'm trying to get in touch with him, if he wants it. Hopefully I can apologise in person and see how he feels.

"I just hope he's OK. That's the most important. I just really care about him right now."

Djokovic - who was defaulted from the 2020 US Open for a similar incident - expressed sympathy for the fan and Medvedev afterwards.

"It's a bit of a shock to be honest. I hope that person is not badly injured," he said.

"I also feel sorry for Daniil. I know exactly how he feels to be disqualified in a big match.

"I am sure that Daniil did not want to do this intentionally."

What is a default in tennis?

Medvedev said afterwards he was "terribly sorry" for the incident

Defaults in tennis are rare and only occur when players violate the sport's code of conduct.

Violations include ball abuse, physical or verbal abuse, or racquet abuse. Players can receive three code violations and then be disqualified if they receive another, but Medvedev's offence was serious enough to instantly default him.

He will now lose the points and prize money he had earned in Beijing.

The 30-year-old is a combustible character who has struggled to control his emotions throughout his career.

He had a meltdown at last year's US Open when a photographer walked on court, and was fined almost £31,500 ($42,500) for his behaviour.

In April, he obliterated a racquet after losing 6-0 6-0 at the Monte Carlo Masters and was again fined for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Medvedev told BBC Sport in 2025 that he was attempting to work on his on-court behaviour.

"When I'm on the court I hate to lose; I love to win. My first goal is to win the match, so it brings a lot of adrenaline out and it brings all the energy out," he said.

"Sometimes it is a good energy. Sometimes it is a bad one."

The default brought an early end to an excellent contest, with 39-year-old Djokovic having played superbly to outlast an opponent nine years his junior.

Djokovic saved 16 of the 18 break points he faced and will go on to play Alex de Minaur in Tuesday's final.

Djokovic has a 33-0 record at the China Open, having won the title six times.

He has won at least one title a year since 2006 - but Tuesday will be his first final since the Australian Open, where he lost to then world number one Carlos Alcaraz in four sets.

He reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon, losing to eventual champion Jannik Sinner, but lost in the third round of the French Open before suffering a shock first-round exit at the US Open.

Elsewhere, defending champion Alcaraz overcame fluctuations in form to beat Jaume Munar and reach the Japan Open final.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion struggled on serve throughout but gradually upped his level to win 5-7 6-3 6-1.

Spain's Alcaraz led 5-3 in the first set and served for it before losing 16 consecutive points to squander the opener.

He will face Jiri Lehecka in the final after the Czech beat Monaco's Valentin Vacherot 6-4 6-2.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
