World.title: Adeleke signs Osun park Management Bill into law amid opposition from APC
World.content:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has signed the state’s Park Management Bill into law, after persistent violence over control of motor parks prompted his administration to suspend activities of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW) and announce plans for a new management system.

Mr Adeleke signed the legislation on Monday at the Government House in Osogbo, saying it would address what he described as longstanding challenges in the state’s transport park system and modernise the sector.

“Having signed this bill into law, I assure all stakeholders that implementation will commence in earnest. In line with the law, we will ensure that Osun people and other interests are accommodated for efficient service delivery across the state,” Mr Adeleke said while signing the Bill.

“I applaud the House Speaker and members of the House for always acting in the best interest of the state. I have gone through the bill as passed by the House and I am convinced that it is the best solution to the perennial crisis and challenges facing the Osun transportation park system,” the governor added.

The Osun State House of Assembly passed the bill on 23 September during its proceedings and forwarded it to Mr Adeleke for assent.

However, the signing of the bill comes amid a constitutional dispute over the authority of the state government to regulate and manage motor parks.

The earlier passage of the legislation had generated opposition from the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun State, which argued that the state legislature lacked the constitutional authority to take over the regulation and management of motor parks.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The party relied on Section 7(1) and the Fourth Schedule of the Nigerian constitution, arguing that the administration and revenue collection associated with public motor parks fall under the functions of democratically elected local government councils.

It warned that implementing the legislation could create further conflict in the state and called for its withdrawal.

However, the House of Assembly rejected the argument. The lawmakers said the APC was relying on a selective interpretation of the constitution and argued that the fact that motor parks are listed among local government functions does not automatically remove the matter from the legislative competence of a state House of Assembly.

The assembly also cited Section 100 of the constitution, which sets out the procedure for exercising the legislative powers of a state House of Assembly through bills passed by the legislature and assented to by the governor.

It challenged the APC to approach the courts if the party believed the legislation was unconstitutional.

“If the APC genuinely believes that the law is unconstitutional, the courts are open to it,” the Assembly said.

House Speaker Adewale Egbedun, who spoke before the signing of the bill on Monday, said the assembly complied with its standing rules in processing and passing the bill and described the legislation as providing answers to concerns surrounding the state’s transport sector.

The crisis that prompted bill

The latest development follows months of tension and violence linked to disputes over control of motor parks in Osun.

On 14 September, Mr Adeleke banned NURTW activities in the state after Olalekan Oyeyemi, popularly known as Emir Ajagungbade, an associate of the governor and Accord Party chief, was shot dead at Mayfair motor park in Ile-Ife.

Mr Oyeyemi was also involved in the transport sector and had served on a government-appointed transport committee. The Osun State Police Command subsequently recovered another corpse from the park in Ile-Ife.

Following the killings, the governor directed rival groups involved in the leadership dispute to vacate motor parks and garages across the state and ordered security agencies to arrest those allegedly involved in the incident.

He also announced plans to reintroduce a Park Management System, initially saying he would issue an executive order to establish the new system.

Meanwhile, the state government in July had suspended NURTW activities in motor parks following a violent confrontation between rival factions. The government maintained that the union’s recognised leadership remained in place, while the national NURTW leadership rejected the suspension and later inaugurated a caretaker committee for the state.

The state government rejected the caretaker committee, insisting that there was no leadership vacuum in the Osun chapter.

PREMIUM TIMES also reported in August that two people were killed during a violent confrontation at the Naira and Kobo area of Ikire, Irewole Local Government Area, in an alleged attempt by a faction to take control of a garage.

World.title: Olise powers France to win over Belgium in Nations League
World.content:
France’s midfielder #11 Michael Olise celebrates after scoring his team’s fourth goal during the UEFA Nations League Group A1 football match between France and Belgium at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, on October 5, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP)

Michael Olise came off the bench to inspire France to a 4-1 win over Belgium in the UEFA Nations League on Monday, handing Zinedine Zidane his first home victory since taking charge.

Use up and down arrow keys to resize the meta box pane.

Dodi Lukebakio put Belgium on course for their first competitive win over Les Bleus in 45 years when he fired the visitors in front in the first half at the Stade de France.

But France turned the match on its head in a blistering finish, scoring four times in the final 13 minutes to preserve Zidane’s unbeaten start and move closer to the quarter-finals.

Desire Doue hauled France level in the 77th minute with a low drive from the edge of the area before Olise teed up Rayan Cherki to fire them ahead four minutes later.

Olise then put the result beyond doubt with a third goal before adding another in stoppage time to cap a stunning French comeback.

France, who also beat Belgium 1-0 in Brussels last week thanks to a late Olise goal, moved three points clear of Italy at the top of Group A1, with Belgium another point back. Italy beat Turkey 3-1 in Bologna to condemn their opponents to a fourth straight loss.

Former World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Zidane heavily rotated his team for the last match of this two-week long international window, with only Dembele keeping his place among the 10 changes.

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Toulouse goalkeeper Guillaume Restes made their France debuts, with Ousmane Dembele again captaining the side in the absence of the injured Kylian Mbappe.

Belgium were without the suspended duo of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans but caught France cold when Romeo Lavia’s superb ball split open the home defence, allowing Lukebakio to race clear and tuck away a clinical finish.

Maarten Vandevoordt, making his debut in goal for Belgium, kept out efforts from Esteban Lepaul and Cherki as France pressed for an equaliser, but the dam eventually burst.

Doue gathered the ball and shot on the turn, beyond the reach of Vandevoordt, to haul France level. Cherki then turned home a cutback from Olise to give the hosts the lead as the Bayern Munich winger stole the show late on.

Olise scrambled in a third in the 88th minute and rolled in a fourth after skilful work from Doue to complete a remarkable turnaround.

AFP

World.title: Tinubu arrives Abuja after Lagos engagements
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu on Monday evening arrived in Abuja after spending a few days in Lagos following his return to Nigeria from a working vacation in Europe.

The President’s aircraft touched down at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at about 7:45 p.m.

He was received on arrival by the National Security Adviser, NSA, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Director of Protocol at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Ibrahim Sule Dan Agundi, and some senior security officials.

Tinubu’s return to Abuja brings to an end his stay in Lagos, where he had carried out a series of official and political engagements following his return from Europe.

Recall that President Tinubu had returned to Lagos on Tuesday last week from working vacation in Europe, during which he stayed in London and Paris and held meetings with political and business interests.

Speaking briefly with journalists shortly after his arrival in Lagos, Tinubu dismissed concerns over his health and declared himself fit and ready to resume full duties.

“Ready to kick, ready to work. There’s nothing wrong. Rumour will always be emanating from politics, but the facts remain I’m here: healthy, sound and ready to go”, the President had said.

Asked about his vacation, Tinubu simply replied “I enjoyed myself”.

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, who was among senior officials who received him in Lagos, had expressed optimism that the President would return to work with renewed energy after his time away.

While in Lagos, Tinubu participated in activities marking Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary, including the national premiere of MKO, a documentary on the life and democratic struggle of the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola.

The President, accompanied by First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, attended the October 1 screening at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts in Lagos.

The documentary chronicled Abiola’s political journey, the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election and the pro-democracy struggle that followed.

Tinubu also received senior government officials and political leaders during his stay in Lagos, including Vice President Kashim Shettima, who visited him at his residence on Saturday.

After the meeting, Shettima said he had remained in regular contact with the President throughout his stay abroad and described Tinubu as fully engaged with developments in the country.

The Vice President also defended the administration’s economic reforms, saying difficult decisions taken since 2023 were necessary to stabilise the economy and lay the foundation for recovery.

It is expected that Tinubu’s return to Abuja will kick-start his re-election campaigns in different parts of the country.

World.title: Ondo plane crash: No survivors yet, only wreckage, IDs – Gov Aiyedatiwa
World.content:
Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa

By Cynthia Alo

Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa has said no survivor has been recovered from Monday’s military aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of the state, with only wreckage of wings, identity cards and uniforms seen.

Aiyedatiwa said rescue teams are yet to access the main body of the aircraft because it went deep into the swamp.

The governor disclosed this on Monday night during an interview on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme.

He said the aircraft, with 32 persons on board, 25 passengers and seven crew members, was a surveillance aircraft on its way from Benin to Lagos, which lost radio signal at about 9:15 a.m.

He said information got to him at about 10:30 a.m. from the chairman of Ilaje Local Government that residents heard a sound like an air tremor before the aircraft dived into a swamp directly facing the Naval Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda.

“They saw the wreckage from the wings, some ID cards and uniforms indicating it was a military aircraft. The main body went deep into the swamp area. They haven’t been able to search the aircraft itself yet,” he said.

He said naval personnel, local emergency officials, Amotekun and residents moved into the creek with boats immediately the crash occurred, but no living soul was found.

He said the site has been cordoned off, while hospitals in Igbokoda and Okitipupa have been placed on standby with ambulances recently procured for the 18 local governments.

The governor said the Nigerian Air Force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau are investigating and will need to recover the black box to determine the exact cause.

Speaking on the recent elimination of Abdussamad Ohida, a top ISWAP coordinator in Ondo forest, Aiyedatiwa said the clearance operation took place about five days ago after months of top secret surveillance.

He said it was a joint operation involving the DSS, Nigerian Army, British intelligence officers and Amotekun, with no casualties recorded on the side of security forces.

The governor explained that the coordinator took over after his former superior, a Central Nigeria ISWAP leader, was arrested by the DSS in 2023, adding that intelligence was generated from that arrest and from tracking of another leader earlier eliminated by DSS.

He revealed that the criminals carry sophisticated weapons beyond AK-47, including GPMG, and had retaliated when security first launched attack.

“When we launched the first attack, they retaliated. So we had to move back, heavily arm, do serious intelligence and mapping before we re-launched,” he said.

Aiyedatiwa said the role of the UK was provision of intelligence and precision targeting equipment that Amotekun does not have, while Amotekun provided knowledge of terrain because many of its operatives are recruited local hunters.

He said Ondo’s vast forests sharing boundaries with Kogi, Edo, Ekiti and Oyo have become a corridor for criminals fleeing military operations in Kogi and Kwara axis.

According to him, what started as farmer-herder clashes years ago has graduated to terrorism, linking the group to the 2025 December 31 attack on Ipele police station and the 2022 Owo massacre.

On whether the group plans to disrupt 2027 elections, he said their agenda in totality is to kill, destroy and disrupt in any form.

World.title: Nine die in Ogun road crash
World.content:
By James Ogunnaike

No fewer than nine persons lost their lives in a fatal road traffic crash along the JBD/ORE route in Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State on Monday.

According to the statement signed by Afolabi Odunsi, Chief Route Commander and Sector Public Education Officer, FRSC Ogun State Sector Command, the crash occurred at about 4:55 p.m. at the Bethel area within the Ijebu-Ode Unit Command.

According to the FRSC, the crash involved a white Toyota Hiace commercial bus, with registration number 14B-299DT, belonging to Delta Line, and a white Sino Truck commercial vehicle, with registration number AAB162XD, belonging to Bill Gas Solution Ltd.

The nine occupants of the two vehicles were all killed in the crash.

The FRSC said the incident occurred while it was raining and the road pavement was wet.

“Preliminary investigation identified speed violation (SPV) as the probable cause of the crash,” the statement said.

The road safety agency said its rescue team arrived at the scene within two minutes of receiving the report, at about 4:58 p.m.

It added that the bodies of the victims were evacuated and deposited at the General Hospital morgue, Ijebu-Ode, while the vehicles were towed to the Ilese Police Station by the Ilese Police Motor Traffic Division.

The Sector Commander, FRSC Ogun State Command, Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, urged motorists, particularly commercial vehicle operators, to exercise maximum caution while driving in the rain.

Ogunjobi advised motorists to obey speed limits, maintain safe following distances and avoid driving behaviours capable of endangering lives.

He warned that speeding on wet roads was particularly dangerous because reduced tyre grip and visibility could make it difficult for motorists to control their vehicles or stop safely.

The FRSC expressed condolences to the families of the victims and urged all road users to make safety their priority at all times.

World.title: Crash: Tinubu declares three-day mourning for Air Force personnel
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu has declared a three-day national mourning for Air Force personnel who died in the crash of a military plane on Monday.

He also directed that flags should be flown at half-mast throughout the country as a mark of respect to the officers.

President Tinubu had earlier expressed profound sadness over the crash of the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 jet.

The accident occurred near a naval base in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State.

A statement by the presidential spokesman, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, said the aircraft, carrying 25 passengers and seven crew members, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed.

“This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten,”

President Tinubu declared in a condolence message to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and all officers, airmen, and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force.

“The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences.

“I commend the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate search and rescue operation following the accident,” he said.

The Air Force will release the officers’ names after contacting their families.

World.title: Ronaldo resumes Al Nassr training after Portugal camp rift
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Cristiano Ronaldo has returned to Al Nassr training after leaving Portugal’s camp last week amid a dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus.

Al Nassr confirmed the forward’s return on Monday by posting pictures of Ronaldo training with his teammates, with the caption: “The GOAT. In the heart of Najd. At Al Nassr.”

Ronaldo later posted pictures on his official Instagram account, confirming his return to training, with the caption: “🟡🔵”.

The 41-year-old is now preparing for Al Nassr’s next Saudi Pro League fixture against Al Diriyah on Friday, October 9.

His return to club duty comes as efforts continue to resolve the fallout with Portugal, with the Portuguese Football Federation reportedly planning a meeting with Ronaldo in an attempt to repair the relationship between the player, Jesus and the national team.

Vanguard had earlier reported that Jesus and FPF president Pedro Proença followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an unsuccessful attempt to persuade him to remain with Portugal.

Bruno Fernandes has also played down suggestions of a split within the squad, saying there are “no divisions” in the national team and describing Ronaldo as Portugal’s “greatest symbol”.

Portugal subsequently secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals after beating Norway 2-1.

Jesus has since left the door open for Ronaldo’s return, saying the forward can come back to the national team if he wants to.

Ronaldo is now back with Al Nassr as attention turns to his club return.

World.title: Presidential Fertiliser Initiative generates ₦61.58bn savings – FG
World.content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

The Federal Government, on Monday, disclosed that early procurement under the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative has generated ₦61.58 billion in savings as Nigeria targets the delivery of 1.1 million metric tonnes of fertiliser in 2026 amid renewed efforts to boost food production and strengthen the country’s agrifood system.

The disclosure was made by the Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, at the Annual Community of Practice (CoP) Meeting on the implementation of the Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme (CAADP) Kampala Declaration, held yesterday in Maiduguri, Borno State.

Kyari also said the government targets the delivery of 1.1 million metric tonnes of fertiliser in 2026 amid renewed efforts to boost food production and strengthen the country’s agrifood system.

Kyari said the Federal Government, state governments, non-state actors and development partners were working together to translate the Kampala Declaration into concrete action capable of improving food security, strengthening rural economies and building resilience across Nigeria’s agricultural sector.

He said the collaboration had become more urgent as Nigeria begins implementation of the CAADP Kampala Declaration and its Strategy and Action Plan for 2026–2035, which adopts a broader agrifood systems approach covering sustainable production, investment and finance, food and nutrition security, trade, inclusion, resilience and governance.

According to the minister, the Federal Government’s efforts were already yielding results, with reductions of up to 50 per cent in the prices of some essential food commodities, alongside expanded input delivery, rural infrastructure investments and support for smallholder farmers.

“The task now is to sustain these gains and deepen their impact,” Kyari said.

He stressed that closer alignment between the Federal Government, states and development partners was critical to achieving sustainable food security.

“Alignment between the Federal and State Governments and partners is indispensable to sustainable food security and resilient livelihoods.

“That alignment must translate into compatible policies, reliable data, complementary investments and clarity of responsibility for delivery. We need one coherent agrifood system in which national direction and State-level execution reinforce one another,” he said.

The minister said Nigeria’s newly validated 10-Year National Agrifood System Strategy and Action Plan would serve as the vehicle for domesticating the Kampala commitments and harmonising implementation across the country.

He explained that the strategy integrates CAADP Biennial Review indicators into Nigeria’s planning, budgeting and reporting systems, while efforts were underway to align national and state budgets, reduce duplication and channel investments towards agreed priorities.

Kyari also announced that the government was pushing ahead with a new mechanisation drive following the unveiling of the National Agricultural Mechanization Policy and National Agricultural Mechanization Investment Strategy in August.

He said the framework would move the country away from fragmented equipment interventions towards a sustainable mechanisation ecosystem, including plans for a mega tractor assembly plant capable of producing between 2,000 and 4,000 tractors annually.

“We are also expanding all-season production through irrigation, improving access to quality seed, supporting our National Agricultural Research Institutes and strengthening the translation of research into practical solutions for farmers,” the minister said.

He added that the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones were designed to link production areas more effectively with processing facilities and markets, stressing that such investments must be integrated with rural infrastructure, extension services, agricultural finance, nutrition and sustainable management of land and water resources.

On the broader agricultural strategy, Kyari said Nigeria could not afford a one-size-fits-all approach, given the country’s diverse agricultural potentials.

He said the National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Policy recognises the distinct production potentials and natural-resource endowments of Nigeria’s five major agricultural zones.

“Our task is to build on those comparative advantages with adaptable technologies, infrastructure and market linkages, rather than expect every State to produce everything,” he said.

The minister also called for greater participation of women and young people across agricultural value chains, as well as stronger conditions for private investment and development finance.

He challenged state governments to ensure that their agricultural action plans were aligned with the Kampala commitments and national priorities, particularly in rural infrastructure, extension, credit, quality inputs, labour-saving technologies, post-harvest loss reduction and climate-resilient agriculture.

The Governor of Borno State, Prof. Babagana Zulum, represented by his Deputy, Hon. Usman Kadafur, described the meeting as more than a gathering of policymakers, development experts, researchers, farmers and private-sector actors.

He said the Community of Practice should serve as a platform for translating shared experience into practical solutions for Nigeria’s agricultural sector.

“A Community of Practice should not simply be a gathering where ideas are presented and applauded. It should be a platform where experience becomes knowledge, knowledge becomes action, and action produces measurable improvement in the lives of our people”, Zulum said.

Also speaking, the Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy in Nigeria, Dr Karin Jansen, said Germany welcomed Nigeria’s leadership in implementing the CAADP Kampala Agenda and remained committed to supporting the country in moving from commitments to coordinated action.

Jansen said transforming Nigeria’s agrifood system required stronger cooperation between the Federal Government and states, alongside active participation by non-state actors.

She identified the Community of Practice as a critical mechanism for linking national priorities with implementation at the state level, while providing room for knowledge exchange, learning and joint problem-solving.

She said Germany, through the Sustainable Agricultural Systems and Policies (AgSys) project, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), was supporting Nigerian partners to strengthen agricultural policy processes, scale successful approaches and deepen civil society participation.

In his closing remarks, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Aliyu Sabi Abdullahi, said Nigeria’s path to food security depended on states identifying and exploiting their respective comparative advantages.

He warned against the siloed approach of the past, arguing that agricultural development must reflect the specific strengths and potentials of each state.

Abdullahi also stressed the need for greater coordination among government ministries and agencies, particularly those responsible for agriculture, health, environment and rural development.

“The challenges facing our agrifood systems are multidimensional. They require the kind of integrated, multi-sectoral approach that we have championed here.

“The synergy between the Ministries of Agriculture, Health, Environment and Rural Development is not merely a bureaucratic ideal; it is a practical necessity”, he said.

He noted that the relationship between food production, nutrition, environmental sustainability and rural development remained central to Nigeria’s economic prosperity.

The Maiduguri meeting was attended by Commissioners of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries, Health, Environment, Commerce and Rural Development, as well as researchers, farmers, private-sector operators, development partners and other stakeholders in the agricultural sector.

World.title: Court affirms Gbenga Hashim as Accord Party presidential candidate
World.content:
Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim

The Federal High Court sitting in Abuja has affirmed Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim as the presidential candidate of the Accord Party for the 2027 presidential election.

The court’s declaration, on Monday, brings a major legal dispute over the party’s presidential ticket to a decisive conclusion.

Justice Mohammed Umar, in his judgment, dismissed the preliminary objections filed against Hashim’s suit and rejected the purported letter relied upon to communicate the cancellation of the party’s presidential primary to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The court also ordered the Accord Party to upload Hashim’s name to INEC as its presidential candidate, effectively recognising his emergence from the party’s presidential primary held on May 30, 2026.

Hashim had approached the court seeking recognition as the duly nominated presidential candidate of Accord Party, where he maintained that he was the sole aspirant and winner of the May 30, 2026 primary.

His case was argued by Henry Akunebu, SAN, who urged the court to compel the party to recognise Hashim and forward his name to INEC.

Akunebu had challenged the validity and evidential value of documents relied upon to dispute Hashim’s emergence, particularly a purported letter notifying INEC of the cancellation of the presidential primary.

He argued that the alleged cancellation letter lacked the party’s official stamp and imprimatur and questioned the circumstances surrounding its receipt by INEC.

Accord’s position was represented by T.W. Olusesi, who maintained that the presidential primary had been cancelled and that no valid primary produced Hashim as the party’s candidate.

Counsel for INEC, D.J. Gusen, similarly argued that the commission did not monitor the purported primary because it had received notification that the exercise had been cancelled.

Justice Umar, however, dismissed the preliminary objections and rejected the purported cancellation letter, paving the way for the court to recognise the outcome of the May 30 primary.

The judgment follows months of legal contest over the Accord Party presidential ticket and the party’s failure to submit Hashim’s name to INEC despite his claim that he had emerged as the winner of the primary.

Hashim had argued that the party’s refusal to upload his name violated the Constitution, Electoral Act 2026 and relevant INEC regulations and guidelines governing the nomination of political party candidates.

In his originating summons, he asked the court to determine whether Accord Party could validly refuse to upload his name to INEC’s nomination portal after the conduct of a primary in which he emerged as the winner.

He had also sought, in the alternative, an order directing the party to conduct a fresh presidential primary in which he would be allowed to participate.

Hashim maintained throughout the proceedings that he was a registered and financially compliant member of Accord Party, had paid the prescribed ₦50 million presidential nomination fee and contributed ₦7 million towards the party’s electronic membership registration programme.

He also maintained that INEC officials monitored the May 30 primary at which he emerged as the sole aspirant.

In his reaction to the ruling, Hashim dedicated the victory to God and called for reconciliation among stakeholders and party members.

“I give God the Glory for this victory, I dedicate the victory also to all stakeholders and our dear party members and my hardworking legal team. We are grateful to the Judiciary that has done justice on this matter.

“We won’t leave anybody behind…We should all come together and work for the party’s victory in the January 16, 2027 presidential election and all other elections. The march to a New Nigeria has started,” said Hashim.

World.title: The Man Who Conquered the Terrain: A Tribute to Dele Alake at 70
World.content:
By Olabode Opeseitan

At 70, Dr. Henry Dele Alake projects the kind of presence that years of public life either refine or expose. The well-manicured white beard, the carefully settled cap, the glasses that hold his gaze in firm focus, the composed carriage of a man who has spent decades navigating institutions, crises and competing ambitions. He does not announce himself loudly. Yet there is something unmistakably deliberate about his bearing, a quality that suggests preparation before performance and reflection before reaction.

His life has been a sustained rebuke to the idea that serious ability must remain imprisoned in a single profession. Journalism taught him that every human enterprise has a language, and that the first duty of intelligence is to learn it before endeavouring to improve it. The editor moves from law to labour, markets to morality, security to sorrow, learning not everything but enough to distinguish sense from performance. This is how Alake acquired his defining gift: not versatility as a display of range, but the elastic capacity to enter strange terrain, understand its burdens, discover its possibilities and excel without losing his centre.

That apprenticeship began in broadcasting. From Ogun State Radio, where the young graduate learnt the unforgiving disciplines of deadline, accuracy and public attention, he moved to the Lagos State Broadcasting Corporation and helped to establish its sister television station, Lagos Television, LTV 8. Before he became a strategist of national consequence, he had already learnt the practical art of building a platform, organising its message and making it answer to a public larger than itself.

At Concord, amid the anguish and danger that followed the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, this capacity was tested by something more exacting than professional ambition. He belonged to those who suffered for the democracy Nigeria now enjoys. In the orbit of MKO Abiola’s media and democratic struggle, fidelity was neither convenient nor ornamental. It carried real hazard. To remain standing near a cause when the militarised state had made standing costly was to learn, in the body and not merely in theory, that liberty has invoices and history remembers who paid them.

His bond with Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu was forged in that same difficult school. It was sustained not by the easy arithmetic of proximity to power, but by the hard mathematics of shared memory. When the transition returned Nigeria to civil rule in 1999, Alake and his close friend Tunji Bello reportedly urged Tinubu to seek the governorship of Lagos rather than return to the National Assembly. Their reasoning was acute: Tinubu’s contribution to the democratic struggle gave Afenifere, then the South-West’s dominant political and socio-cultural force, a basis on which to rally behind him. They read the political weather correctly, and the forecast became history.

That instinct would define Alake’s work as a communications strategist. He brought the editor’s stern economy to political language, knowing that a message is not strengthened by noise but by structure, timing and proof. In Lagos, in national campaigns and in the management of public argument, he proved unusually alert to the relationship between narrative and power. Where others saw a microphone, he saw the machinery behind it. He understood that the right sentence can clarify a policy, steady a coalition and prevent an opponent from writing the first draft that controls your purpose.

Then came solid minerals, a ministry whose technical vocabulary might have daunted a lesser learner. Alake approached it in the manner that has defined his life: he entered the terrain, studied the files, located the fractures and organised the response. Illegal extraction met the force of the Mining Marshals. A sector long treated as a buried promise began to acquire the architecture of a national priority. The reported rise in revenue from ₦16 billion in 2023 to more than ₦70 billion in 2025, a 337% increase, offered measurable evidence of renewed attention to a neglected sector. Whether every ambition of the reforms is ultimately realised remains to be seen, but mining has acquired a seriousness, visibility and policy coherence that would have seemed unlikely only a few years ago.

The deeper ambition has been to move the conversation beyond extraction and toward value creation. Under the Tinubu administration, with Alake supervising the sector, Nigeria advanced a policy discouraging the export of unprocessed mineral resources and encouraging greater domestic beneficiation.

Lithium-processing projects emerged or advanced in Nasarawa, Kaduna and other locations; multi-billion-dollar investment commitments were announced; and the ministry began to articulate a mining future in which a larger share of the value generated from Nigerian resources is retained within Nigeria. The long-term success of that vision will depend on execution, but the direction of policy is unmistakable.

In September 2026, Alake signed with the United States a framework designed to deepen cooperation and investment across Nigeria’s estimated $700 billion mineral-resource base. Its significance is monumental: it creates a platform for viable projects, commercial partnerships and investment across geological data, exploration, processing, infrastructure and technical capacity. A country is not made wealthy because its soil is full. It becomes wealthy when its institutions learn to listen to the soil.

This, then, is the true distinction of Dele Alake at 70. He has made grit look intelligent, loyalty look strategic and preparation look like destiny. He has been eloquent without vanity, fearless without noise and resourceful without fuss. He did not merely survive the storms of politics; he kept the map dry.

Some men spend their lives searching for favourable ground. Dele Alake built a career by learning to read the terrain beneath everyone’s feet before they knew it had shifted. And wherever that terrain happened to be, the newsroom, the barricades of democracy, the machinery of government or the mineral wealth beneath the soil, he left it more organised, more legible and more consequential than he found it.

*Olabode Opeseitan is a a public affairs analyst

World.title: Tinubu Declares 3-Day Mourning For NAF Personnel Who Died In Plane Crash.
World.content:
Directs flags be flown at half-mast.

Orders thorough investigation of the incident

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has declared a three-day national mourning for Air Force personnel who died in the crash of a military plane near naval base around Igbokoda in Ondo State.



The President, in a release issued on Monday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga also directed that flags should be flown at half-mast nationwide as a mark of respect to the officers.

Tinubu also ordered a comprehensive investigation into the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) ATR-42 jet that crashed near a naval base in Igbokoda area of Ondo State.



The President disclosed that having been briefed by the Chief of Sir Staff, he has directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences.



“I commend the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate Search and Rescue operation following the accident.



“I pray for the repose of the souls of the gallant officers and for Almighty God to grant their families and the Nigerian Air Force the fortitude to bear the unfortunate loss.



“I assure the Nigerian Air Force of the continued support of our administration as they continue their vital role in securing our nation.



“I also commend the swift response of first responders and the Ondo State Government at the crash site”, Tinubu said.



The President expressed profound sadness over the crash of the aircraft which was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred.



Tinubu extended his deepest condolences to the family of the 25 passengers and seven crew members involved, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and all officers, airmen and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force.



“This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten.”

World.title: Defence Minister Mourns Victims of NAF Plane Crash, Condoles Families
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (Rtd), has expressed deep sorrow over the tragic crash of a military aircraft with tail number NAF 931, involving dedicated personnel of the Armed Forces.

In a statement he personally signed, General Musa noted that the painful incident claimed the lives of brave officers and airmen who were engaged in a routine flight mission while serving the nation with courage, unwavering devotion and selfless patriotism.

The loss of these valiant patriots, he said, is an irreparable blow not only to the military high command and their comrades-in-arms, but also to the entire nation.

The Minister said these fine officers and men exemplified the highest standards of military professionalism, loyalty and commitment to the defence of Nigeria.

According to him, “On behalf of the Ministry of Defence, I extend our heartfelt condolences to His Excellency, the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR; the leadership of the Armed Forces; and, most especially, the immediate families, loved ones and colleagues of our fallen heroes.

“We share in your immense grief and stand shoulder-to-shoulder with you during this tragic hour.Our hearts also go out to the families of the civilians on board the ill-fated aircraft. We share your grief.”

He, however, disclosed that a comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate crash had been ordered to ascertain its cause and ensure that all necessary operational safety protocols are reinforced across military aviation units.

“We pray that the Almighty God grants the souls of the departed eternal repose and gives their families, the military community and all Nigerians the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,” he prayed.

World.title: NYSC to Kickstart 2026 Batch “C” Stream ll Orientation November 4
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

The management of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), has announced that the Batch “C” stream ll orientation for youth corps members will commence on November 4, 2026.



The NYSC made this known in a press statement signed by its Director, Information and Public Relations (DIPR), Carolina Embu.



“The Management of National Youth Service Corps has approved Wednesday, 4th November, 2026 as the commencement date for the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream II Orientation Course.



“The exercise will be conducted in all the 36 States and the FCT, Abuja,” she stated

Giving full details of the exercise, Embu said, “Registration of corps members will hold between Wednesday 4th and midnight of Friday 6th November, while the swearing-in ceremony will take place on Friday 6th November, 2026.



“Consequently, the closing ceremony is scheduled to take place on Tuesday 24th November, 2026,” she added.

World.title: Gov AbdulRazaq Splashes N120m on Awardees As Kwara Celebrates World Teachers’ Day
World.content:
Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq on Monday presented awards worth N120 million to “the most outstanding teachers and head teachers/principals” of basic and post-basic public and private schools across the state.

A statement by the Deputy Chief Press Secretary, Government House, Mashood Abdulrafiu Agboola, revealed that the awards, which are in different categories are broken down as follows: 29 best principals/head teachers got N29 million; 119 outstanding teachers got N59,500 million; 11 serving and retired varsity dons won pioneer professorship recognition awards with N22 million, while three schools went home with N9 million for the Best Kept School award.

The governor also announced his government’s plan to buy 10,000 shares of the Dangote Refinery IPO for 10 female teachers in each of the outstanding public schools, saying the motive was to foster investment culture among them.

Governor AbdulRazaq, who identified teachers as major drivers in the sector, said his government will continually prioritise their welfare in the state.

He added that the award was to recognise their sacrifice and motivate them to do more.

“We will continue to do our part, including improving your welfare and working conditions on a sustainable basis. We are confident that you and other stakeholders will always do your part,” the governor said in Ilorin after making a symbolic presentation of the prizes at an event to commemorate the World Teachers’ Day.

“Our objective remains clear: to build an education system that gives every child in Kwara a fair opportunity to learn, develop useful skills and compete anywhere in the world. The quality of education we provide today will determine the quality of Kwara we have tomorrow.

“When we came into office, we knew that improving the education sector was a top priority. We also knew that this required more than building classrooms or increasing the number of teachers. We needed to improve the quality of teaching and learning itself as well as sustainably restore the dignity of our teachers.

“That informed our decision to recruit qualified teachers through a merit-based process, strengthen continuous professional development, improve school infrastructure and introduce technology and data into the management of basic education through KwaraLEARN.”

AbdulRazaq also spoke about the regular promotion of teachers and the implementation of the 27.5 % Teachers’ Specific Allowance (TSA) by the administration, acknowledging that the “welfare and honour of our teachers must remain a priority at all times”.

According to him, government’s interventions in the sector are already yielding results considering the superlative performance of the school pupils that have earned the state many laurels at national and international competitions.

Talking about Dangote shares, the governor disclosed that he has directed the state Head of Service, Dr. Olufunke Mercy Shittu, to design modalities to capture outstanding retired female teachers under the Dangote Refinery IPO as well.

“Before I conclude, we have been in discussion with Dangote Foundation and this discussion is about promoting investment culture among women, financial inclusion, investment, assets and shareholding,” he said.

“Dangote has created the Dangote Foundation, providing subscription grounds for women only. For every 10 shares we purchase they will give a grant of another 10 shares making 20 shares.

“Our hardworking women teachers in TESCOM and SUBEB will get 10 shares each. We will also extend it to the retired female teachers so that peace and prosperity will go round them.”

At the event were top government officials, National President, Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Comrade Audu Titus Amba represented by Issa Habeeb, state leaders of NUT, heads of educational institutions, APC party leaders, and leaders of labour unions.

APC deputy governorship candidate in the state, Hon Seun Oguniyi Adato, ìn his remarks, said there are many instances to cite on how the governor has added values to the teaching profession and the lives of teachers in the state.

He congratulated the teachers worldwide and indeed in Kwara State on the celebration.

Dr Lawal Olohungbebe, the state Commissioner for Education and Human Capital Development, for his part, said hard work deserves to be recognised.

He congratulated the awardees on their pick, while charging them to keep the flag high.

He encouraged teachers in the state to continue to develop themselves and remain focused on the most important outcomes that every child learns, assuring them that the ministry will keep engaging with relevant stakeholders on issues affecting the welfare of teachers, professional development and their working conditions.

Chairman, State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB), Prof. Sheu Raheem Adaramaja, said the state government has given them an approval for the conduct of the 2026 promotion for teachers, announcing that the promotion exam has been scheduled for next Saturday.

Adaramaja, who is also the Dean of State Chairmen for SUBEB, said Kwara will be the first state to conduct 2026 promotion exercise for eligible teachers in the whole federation.

Former Chairman of NLC in Kwara State and keynote speaker, Comrade Umar Farooq, urged the government and other critical stakeholders to continue to create conditions that will enable teachers to succeed.

He noted that supporting teachers is not merely supporting a profession but should be seen as an investment in the children, communities and society that depend on them.

Earlier, the state NUT Chairman, Comrade Yusuf Wahab Agboola, commended the government for its investments in school infrastructure and the well-being of teachers through various initiatives.

He requested the government to key into the national harmonised retirement age for teachers, among other requests.

World.title: NIBSS Fraud Desk Highlights PalmPay Security Measures Amid Evolving Fraud Risks
World.content:
The Head of the Fraud Management Department at the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) Plc, Tosin Obadimu, has highlighted security measures available to PalmPay customers through the company’s upgraded Security Center.

The Security Center brings account and transaction protection features into one platform, including Security Check, Large Transaction Shield, Night Guard, USSD account and card lock, and alerts relating to suspected fraud recipients, duplicate transfers and new-device logins.

According to Obadimu, the combination of these controls can support additional verification around higher-risk transactions and improve the process for reporting and tracking fraud incidents.

“PalmPay’s upgraded Security Center brings account and transaction protection into a single hub, combining a real-time Security Check with user-configurable safeguards such as Large Transaction Shield, Night Guard, USSD account and card lock, and in-flow alerts for suspected fraud recipients, duplicate transfers and new-device logins,” he said.

“From an industry perspective, these controls strengthen verification before high-risk transactions against social engineering and account takeover, while the integrated dispute, fraud reporting and case-tracking features should speed up incident reporting and improve fund recovery across the ecosystem.”

The comments come as fraud methods continue to include impersonation, social engineering and unauthorised access to customer accounts. These methods can involve fraudsters posing as financial institutions or other trusted entities to obtain sensitive information or persuade customers to approve transactions.

Samuel Oluyemi, Chief Operating Officer of PalmPay Nigeria, said customer protection measures need to change as fraud methods and digital financial services evolve.

“With my over two and a half decades in Nigeria’s payments ecosystem, I understand that fraud management requires continuous innovation and empathy for the customer above profitability. As customers’ financial services needs evolve, so must the techniques of customer protection against fraud and unauthorised transactions improve,” he said.

PalmPay said fraud prevention involves financial institutions, payment providers, regulators and customers. The company said it would continue to review its security measures in response to emerging fraud risks.

World.title: Foundation, DAWN Commission Pledge to Sustain Akeredolu’s Push for State Police
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The Development Agenda for Western Nigeria (DAWN) Commission and Oluwarotimi Akeredolu Foundation, have assured of their commitment to the realization of state policing as advocated for by the former governor of Ondo state, late Arakunrin Oluwarotimi Akeredolu, during his life time.

The two bodies as part of programnes lined up to mark his 70th posthumous birthday will be organizing a colloquium with the theme, “Fundamentals and Governance of State Policing: Towards a New Architecture for National Security in Nigeria,”

The event is expected to bring together governors, lawmakers, security chiefs, traditional rulers, academics and civil society actors to discuss the future of policing and national security in Nigeria.

A representative of the Akeredolu family, Mr. Taiwo Adewole, while speaking with journalists in Ibadan, said the family choose to celebrate the late governor through ideas and conversations around issues he championed during his lifetime.

According to him, Akeredolu, who would have turned 70 on July 21, 2026, was a lawyer, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, former President of the Nigerian Bar Association and two-term governor of Ondo State, describing him as “a man of courage,” who spoke when silence was safer, acted when waiting was easier and stood up when others sat down.

Adewole said Akeredolu remained committed to the security and welfare of the people, particularly during periods of insecurity in the South-West.

“When farmers were killed on their farms, he did not look away. When criminals made our forests their hiding places, he drew a line. When terror came to Owo, his own hometown, he stood with his people and grieved with them,”

He recalled that as Chairman of the South-West Governors’ Forum, Akeredolu played a leading role in the establishment of Operation Amotekun, despite opposition and doubts from some quarters.

“He believed security begins at home. He believed the people closest to a community are best placed to protect it,” he said.

Adewole added that the family had chosen not to mourn Akeredolu with tears alone but to honour him by continuing conversations around the ideas and causes he championed.

The Director-General of the DAWN Commission, Dr. Seye Oyeleye, on his part, said the commission was proud to convene the Aketi@70 Colloquium in partnership with the Oluwarotimi Akeredolu Foundation.

According to him, the event scheduled for Thursday, October 8, at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan, is aimed at keeping alive Akeredolu’s contributions to the debate on state policing and national security.

He said Nigeria’s security challenges, including banditry, kidnapping, farmer-herder clashes and attacks on farms, highways and places of worship, had made the debate on policing increasingly important, noting that Nigeria’s centralised policing structure is under strain, making it necessary to have a serious conversation about how state policing can be implemented, funded, regulated and made accountable.

“The debate on state policing is no longer about whether. It is about how. How do we fund it? How do we train and equip it? How do we guard against abuse? How do we keep it accountable to the people, not to politicians?

“These are the questions this colloquium will tackle,” he said.

Oyeleye said the discussion is not a regional or Yoruba agenda but a national issue that went to the heart of Nigeria’s federal structure.

He said the experience of Operation Amotekun has demonstrated the potential of regional cooperation and the importance of local knowledge in addressing security challenges.

“Amotekun showed what is possible. Regional cooperation works. Local knowledge saves lives,”

He urged Nigerians and the media to participate actively in the discourse, stating that Akeredolu’s death should not mark the end of the ideas and conversations he started.

“Honouring Aketi is not about the past. It is about the Nigeria we must build,” Oyeleye added.

World.title: Tinubu Returns To Abuja After Six-Day Visit To Lagos
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu will depart Lagos for Abuja on Monday evening after his six-day visit to the former seat of government.

The President had arrived in Lagos on Tuesday, September 29, after spending his annual vacation in London and Paris.

Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, in a release, stated that while in Lagos, Tinubu addressed the nation on 1st October to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day anniversary.

Later that day, he attended the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts for the National Premiere of MKO, a documentary that chronicles the life, political struggle, and enduring legacy of the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Abiola and the historic June 12 pro-democracy struggle.

The President also, on Sunday, paid a visit to the Oba of Lagos, Oba Rilwan Babatunde Akiolu, at his Iga Iduganran Palace on Lagos Island.

World.title: Roosevelt High School principal condemns disastrous Matric Dance
World.content:
The principal of Roosevelt High School ha publicly condemned the behaviour of learners at the recent Matric Dance. Image via Canva

The principal of Roosevelt High School in Johannesburg has published a stern open letter condemning the disastrous events that took place at the school’s recent Matric Dance.

The event – held at the upmarket Avianto Hotel – was cut short after pupils arrived under the influence of alcohol and drugs, threatened staff with firearms and left the venue in an “unacceptable condition”.

ROOSEVELT HIGH SCHOOL PRINCIPAL CONDEMNS DRUNK, DRUGGED GRADE 12 LEARNERS

In a lengthy open letter posted on the school’s official Facebook page, Roosevelt High School principal Cristèl Venter expressed her shock and disappointment at the behaviour of some learners who attended the Matric Dance at the Avianto Hotel in Muldersdrift.



Venter had initially skipped the event due to illness, but had been called in to intervene after things took a turn for the worse.

Venter revealed that learners had arrived under the influence of alcohol and drugs, and had threatened staff with firearms during their rowdy procession and reckless driving into the venue. Intoxicated learners became violently ill, vomiting all over the five-star venue.

The principal decided to cut short the Matric Dance in a bid to de-escalate the deteriorating situation, but was met with contempt and verbal abuse from parents, who angrily confronted school staff.



She shared: “In my 19 years at Roosevelt High School, I cannot recall another evening in which I apologised as many times as I did that night…to venue personnel, to staff, and to some learners who had done absolutely nothing wrong”.

The principal vowed to launch an investigation and disciplinary proceedings into the event, vowing to take action against individuals “lawfully, fairly and in accordance with due process”

“Where misconduct is established, there will be accountability.



Venter urged parents to enforce “manners, boundaries, respect for other people and understanding that actions have consequences”

She added, “The behaviour witnessed and reported last night will not become normal at Roosevelt High School. We can and must do better”.

CALLS FOR STRICT REGULATION OVER MATRIC DANCES

On the Facebook page, Roosevelt High School reposted a video by podcaster Penuel Mlostshwa, who weighed in on the school’s disastrous Matric Dance.



Mlotshwa urged South African schools and parents to regulate Matric Dance events, curbing unnecessary expenditure and financial pressure on parents.

He shared: “There is a lot of pressure on kids and their parents to buy very expensive clothing, and sadly, this now becomes a show off”

Penuel proposed that grade 12 learners enjoy a farewell event on school premises, during school hours, and wearing school uniforms.



“No fancy cars or parades”, he added.

World.title: New chapter: Durban’s Nenezane Hair Studios moves to Joburg!
World.content:
Snenhlanhla Mthembu, the owner of Nenezane Hair Studios, announced via Instagram on 1 October 2026 that her popular establishment is officially making the move to Johannesburg.

The Durban-based salon has attracted “amazing women” over the years, including celebrities such as Mawhoo, Sithelo Shozi, and Ntando Duma, who have trusted the brand for premium wig installations.

NENEZANE HAIR STUDIOS IS MOVING TO JOBURG

The salon will officially unplug its hairdryers and tongs on 25 November 2026, marking a brand-new chapter in Johannesburg from 1 December 2026.



The move to the City of Gold ushers in growth for the business, which has enjoyed a successful five-year run in Durban.

Snenhlanhla expressed her heartfelt gratitude to all her clients for their unwavering support and trust throughout the years.

“For the past 5 years since I started this journey of wig installations, you have been my rock. You supported me when I had nothing; you never left my side; you referred your sisters, your friends, your mothers to me,” she wrote.

“You trusted me with your crowns, you celebrated my wins with me, and you lifted me on my hard days. Because of you, Nenezane Hair Studios became what it is today,” she added.

FROM DURBAN TO JOBURG

For Snenhlanhla, Durban isn’t merely a place of business; it is also home. Therefore, it is not easy to simply pack up and leave, considering the invaluable connections she has forged there.

However, the move also presents an uncertain yet exciting future, one she hopes God will guide her through.



“Leaving Durban is not easy. I have built so much more than a business here. I have built a family,” she wrote.

She added, “I have met the most amazing women and will forever cherish every appointment, every laugh, every conversation we had in my chair.”

“Thank you from the bottom of my heart for your love, your loyalty, and your support. I will never take it for granted,” she continued.

“As I move to Johannesburg, I am moving to start a brand-new chapter. 1 am scared, but I am hopeful that I will go and make the most of this opportunity. I am praying that God goes before me and opens doors for me in Joburg just like He did for me here in Durban,” she added.

GOOD NEWS FOR DURBAN CLIENTS

Luckily for her beloved clients in Durban, the relocation is not the end of Snenhlanhla’s services, as they can still order wigs online, and she will take bookings whenever she is in the city.

World.title: IFP vows to tackle illegal immigration at municipal level
World.content:
Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) mayoral candidate for the eThekwini Municipality Mkhuleko Hlengwa says municipalities do not deal directly with illegal immigration, but South Africa’s current immigration crisis requires the issue to be addressed at municipal level.

Hlengwa was speaking to party members during the IFP’s eThekwini manifesto launch at the Hollywoodbets Greyville Racecourse on Sunday, 4 October.

IFP VOWS TO DEAL WITH ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION

During his address, Hlengwa said the party plans to tackle illegal immigration to ensure that eThekwini works for Durban residents and South Africans.



He said the municipality would work with other government stakeholders to address illegal immigration, while also tackling crime, human trafficking and drugs.

“The deportation of people who are in the country illegally is not something that a municipality deals with, however, the crisis in South Africa forces municipalities to deal with it. By working hand in hand with other government stakeholders, we will make sure that whoever is here [in South Africa] is here legally. If they’re not legal, they should go.”

Hlengwa said the party’s approach would be aimed at protecting the local economy and young people from what he described as the impact of drugs and human trafficking.

“We will do this to preserve the eThekwini economy, protect the youth from drugs which are brought by foreign nationals, protect women and children from rape and human trafficking by foreign nationals. We will do this because South Africans should be put first and eThekwini residents should be put first,” Hlengwa said.

IMMIGRATION REMAINS CONTENTIOUS ISSUE

The IFP’s comments come as immigration remains a contentious issue in South Africa, with concerns about undocumented migrants and pressure on public services continuing to feature prominently in political and public debate.

Anti-illegal immigration groups, including March and March, have intensified their campaigns calling for undocumented migrants to be deported.



The Department of Home Affairs has also previously said that people should not be denied access to its services solely because they are in the country illegally, while immigration enforcement and deportation remain matters handled by national government.

Hlengwa said the IFP would work with relevant government departments to ensure that immigration laws are enforced while prioritising the interests of eThekwini residents.

World.title: Sipho Mbule reveals why he turned down Kaizer Chiefs

Mbule was out of contract with Sundowns last year and eventually made the move to their rivals Orlando Pirates.

The midfielder spent just one season with the Buccaneers, making 23 appearances across all competitions before leaving the club and joining Iraqi side Zakho SC.



Speaking on the Giants documentary, Mbule explained why he chose Pirates despite interest from several clubs, including Chiefs.

“Firstly, my contract with Sundowns ended. There were other teams that also wanted to sign me. Even Chiefs approached me,” Mbule said.

“The people and coaches that I spoke to, like coach Rulani, told me that the best team to join is Pirates because I think there was an opportunity for him to make a comeback [to the team].”

Mbule quickly became a fan favourite at Pirates, but his time at the club was ultimately cut short and his contract was not renewed.

His struggles at club level also affected his international career, with the midfielder losing his place in the Bafana Bafana setup and subsequently missing out on the FIFA World Cup.

Mbule was loved by Pirates fans

The “Master Chef” has since revived his career in Iraq, where he appears to have rediscovered his best form.



His resurgence at Zakho SC will come as a welcome boost for a player who was once regarded as one of the most talented midfielders in South African football.

World.title: Former PSL star pleads guilty to culpable homicide, sentencing set
World.content:
The charges against the PSL star relate to a collision on 30 October 2024. It claimed the life of nine-year-old Gomolemo Mavimbela and left two other people seriously injured.

Appearing in the Tembisa Magistrate’s Court, Mogaila admitted in his plea statement that he had negligently caused the collision. According to the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA), his vehicle veered into oncoming traffic on Andrew Mapheto Road before colliding with another vehicle.

PSL STAR SHAUNE MOGAILA ADMITS TO CAUSING FATAL CRASH

The devastating collision resulted in the death of Gomolemo Mavimbela, while her mother and 13-year-old brother were seriously injured.



NPA Communications Officer Magaboke Mohlatlole confirmed that the guilty plea resulted in a conviction on the charges of culpable homicide and failure to render assistance.

“The conviction follows a fatal collision on Andrew Mapheto Road in Tembisa on 30 October, 2024 when Mogaila’s vehicle veered into oncoming traffic and collided with another vehicle,” Mohlatlole said.

“The crash claimed the life of nine year old, Gomolemo Mavimbela, and left her mother and 13 year old brother seriously injured.

“The NPA welcomes tge conviction as an important step towards securing justice for the victims. Mogaila’s bail has been extended until his next court appearance on 17 November 2026, when he’s expected to be sentenced.”

The AfriForum Private Prosecution Unit had previously opposed proposals that could have resulted in a more lenient outcome for Mogaila. Its spokesperson, Barry Bateman, also expressed disappointment that the former PSL player did not provide a fuller account of his actions leading up to the crash.

SENTENCING SET FOR NOVEMBER

Although the PSL star has now been convicted, the case is not yet over, with sentencing scheduled for 17 November 2026. The former Sekhukhune United player remains out on R20,000 bail, which has been extended until his next appearance.



The NPA said Mogaila is expected to return to the Tembisa Magistrate’s Court on the sentencing date.

The case has brought renewed attention to the consequences of the fatal Thembisa crash, with the family of Gomolemo Mavimbela having lost a nine-year-old child while two other family members suffered serious injuries.

World.title: Why Zimbabwe is suddenly back on Trump’s radar
World.content:
President Trump to send delegation to Zimbabwe. Image via X@FonsiLoaiza

Zimbabwe is suddenly attracting renewed attention from Washington, with United States President Donald Trump expected to send a delegation to Harare for talks with President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

The potential visit follows a meeting between Mnangagwa and Republican Congressman Marlin Stutzman on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month.

According to Zimbabwean officials, Stutzman subsequently briefed Trump on his discussions with Mnangagwa, leading to the proposal for a congressional and business delegation to Zimbabwe.



But why is Zimbabwe back on the US radar?

Zimbabwe’s critical minerals

One major factor is Zimbabwe’s mineral wealth.

The country is seeking to position itself as an important player in the global energy transition, particularly through the extraction and local processing of minerals required for modern industries.



Zimbabwe has significant deposits of lithium, platinum-group metals, nickel and chrome, among other minerals.

Zimbabwe has increasingly pushed for investment in local processing rather than simply exporting raw minerals, creating opportunities for foreign companies seeking access to strategic mineral supplies.

This could make Zimbabwe an increasingly important economic partner as countries compete for secure critical-mineral supply chains.



Zimbabwe’s new US trade opening

Trade is another reason for the renewed engagement.

The United States has included Zimbabwe in its fiscal 2027 tariff-rate quota for raw cane sugar, giving the country an allocation of 813 metric tonnes.

The quota allows qualifying sugar imports to enter the US at a lower tariff rate than quantities outside the quota.



The move places Zimbabwe alongside other African countries, including South Africa, Mozambique and Malawi, which also have allocations under the US sugar programme.

While the allocation is relatively small, it provides Zimbabwean producers with an opportunity to access the American market.

Zimbabwe’s long-running sanctions issue

The potential thaw also comes against the background of Zimbabwe’s more than two decades of difficult relations with Washington.



The Zimbabwe Democracy and Economic Recovery Act (ZDERA), passed in 2001, has long been a major point of contention between the two countries.

A US bill proposing the repeal of ZDERA has also been introduced, although any change to the legislation would require the US legislative process to run its course.

For Zimbabwe, improved relations with Washington could therefore have implications far beyond diplomacy.



What happens next?

Zimbabwe and US officials have indicated that high-level visits, trade and investment are among the issues being discussed.

If the proposed delegation travels to Harare, attention will turn to whether the engagement produces concrete deals on minerals, agriculture, investment and trade.

For now, the developments suggest that Washington and Harare are exploring a more commercially focused relationship after years of strained ties.

World.title: When to record? Expert weighs in on how cellphone videos can become crucial evidence
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Cellphones are more than just devices used for communication and social media.

At the right moment, that phone can become a powerful tool for recording acts of crime or even misconduct.

This footage can ultimately play a crucial role in criminal or even disciplinary cases.

An example of this is the case against Lawrence Mudzinganyama.

Mudzinganyama was captured on camera allegedly threatening to shoot and kill a group of women at an upmarket Sandton restaurant.

He now faces ten charges, including fraud, intimidation and crimen injuria.

READ | Businessman accused of threatening women at Sandton restaurant granted bail

But his case is one of many.

There is also the case of eight Milnerton High School pupils who were charged with assault after a disturbing video has surfaced showing a 16-year-old Cape Town pupil being brutally assaulted.

READ| UPDATE: Eight Milnerton High pupils appear in court

For social media law expert Emma Sadlier, the ability to capture such scenes proves one's courage to document serious misconduct when it happens because, without that evidence, it may be hard to act against the perpetrator.

“We just see electronic evidence permeate the courtroom, and I think that the more that evidence exists, the more bad people end up facing the full might of the law; as a result of that evidence being taken, I say all the better,” she said.

In addressing the issue of privacy, Sadlier explained that once evidence is manifestly in the public interest, then one should not worry about the privacy rights of an individual.

She does, however, caution that there are two instances when a person's privacy is infringed.

“The first is consent, and the second is if it benefits the public. What I say is a rule of thumb, in short, when you do something illegal, when you do something against the law, against the rules, your privacy falls out the window.”

The issue becomes more sensitive when it comes to children if they are involved.

Sadlier said that in those events, it is important to be mindful of the privacy rights of children.

World.title: Number Of The Day | 100 million | 05 October 2026
World.content:
100 Million Barrels Sounds Huge. In A Global Oil Crisis, It May Not Be

One hundred million barrels of oil sounds like the kind of number that should move markets.

That is precisely what the G7 hopes will happen. Its members have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency crude oil and refined fuel reserves, with an early emphasis on diesel, as governments try to contain soaring energy costs and restore confidence to a market shaken by war, disrupted supply routes and shortages of refined products.

But the size of a government intervention tells only part of the story. What matters is the scale of the disruption it is trying to offset.

In a recent Number of the Day discussion, Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd put that imbalance into perspective. Citing International Energy Agency figures discussed during the episode, they noted that about 4.3 million barrels a day had been taken off the market. Using a conservative four-million-barrel daily figure over

seven months, the episode arrives at roughly 840 million barrels removed from supply; dramatically larger than the new 100-million-barrel intervention.

That does not make the G7 release insignificant. It helps explain why its effect may be limited.

The Problem Is Bigger Than Crude Oil

Oil markets are not simply a question of how many barrels exist underground or in strategic reserves. Consumers do not put crude oil into their cars. Crude must be transported, refined into products such as petrol and diesel, shipped to the markets that need it and delivered through functioning supply chains.

That distinction has become increasingly important during the current crisis. The G7 plan includes refined products, particularly diesel, precisely because shortages have developed further down the supply chain. European economies, for example, rely partly on imported diesel to supplement domestic refinery output, while disruption elsewhere has intensified competition for available cargoes.

The podcast captures the problem neatly through another number: global oil inventories stood at about 7.8 billion barrels in August, according to the IEA figure cited in the conversation. Yet much of that supply may be in pipelines, storage or locations from which it cannot quickly reach the places experiencing shortages.

In other words, availability is not the same as accessibility.

A market can simultaneously contain billions of barrels of oil and still experience acute shortages of the right product, in the right place, at the right time.

South Africa Cannot Escape The Global Price

For South Africans, this distinction is no academic exercise.

The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources confirmed that new fuel prices will take effect on 7 October. During the review period, the average Brent crude price rose from $87.89 to $101 a barrel. Government attributed the increase to geopolitical tensions, uncertainty around oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, higher shipping costs and falling inventories.

South Africa is particularly exposed because it imports crude oil and finished petroleum products whose prices are determined internationally. The monthly domestic fuel-price calculation therefore absorbs both the international product price and movements in the rand.

That combination is now painful. Reuters reported that petrol prices are set to rise by as much as 12%, while wholesale diesel increases by about 10%.

The G7's 100-million-barrel intervention may eventually help ease some pressure. But emergency reserves cannot immediately repair damaged supply chains, remove geopolitical risk, restore refining capacity or strengthen the rand.

That is why the real significance of the number is not simply that 100 million barrels are being released.

It is that even 100 million barrels can look small when the problem is bigger than the stockpile.

References

· Number of the Day, Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd, 05 October 2026.

· South African Government, fuel-price adjustment effective 7 October 2026.

· Associated Press, G7 emergency oil and diesel release, 2 October 2026.

· The Guardian, G7 coordinated emergency reserve release, 2 October 2026.

· Reuters, South African October fuel-price increase, 5 October 2026.
