Joining Brian Lilley are Chris Varcoe, Postmedia’s western business columnist, and Lorne Gunter, political columnist. They discuss the likelihood of this pipeline ever happening, the battles yet to fight, the eye-watering costs and the dismaying timeline before it gets done. They also discuss Smith’s feat in pushing the Liberals to overturn the last prime minister’s anti-oil dogmas. But given Carney’s costly carbon-capture conditions and other roadblocks, simply declaring a “national interest” won’t be enough to make Alberta’s oilpatch great again.

World.title: Book Review: Patrick deWitt’s mastery as a writer is revealed in Giller-nominated Dodge City
World.content:
Article content

The Canadian author’s immaculately crafted sixth novel, is a tender story that begins in 1967, when Lee, 23, a broke, small-town expat, kind of in love, kind of happy, while navigating a new sunlit life in L.A., coolly punches out some rich kid who’s got it coming and gets expelled from UCLA. Soon after, he gets drafted, and confronted with the “lunatic reality” of the induction office, decides to flee to Canada rather than fight in Vietnam — this is fight and flight of a different sort.

World.title: ‘People do suffer from weirdness’: Canadian author Patrick deWitt reinvents the comedy of manners
World.content:
Article content

Hence, deWitt’s new novel, Dodge City, is predictably alert to the bizarre realities of human behaviour. For example, we don’t feel that we’re entering fantasyland when we arrive at an oddball portrait of an aging dogcatcher who resorts to highly unorthodox methods to keep his job. Such scenes are laced with deWitt’s trademark humour — but they’re accompanied by a tenderness and warmth that’s characteristic of deWitt’s zest for pulling off tricky balancing acts in his fiction. He can be a breeze to read: to write about him is more complicated. Peel away one layer and there’s another to confound you. When it comes to his literary credentials, a thoroughly contemporary sensibility finds nurture in the past. Go figure.
