World.title: Iraq pledges $2.7 billion to stimulate economic growth
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi directed on Sunday an executive funding package and measures totaling 3.5 trillion Iraqi dinars ($2.7 billion).

The comprehensive economic program is tailor-made to increase market liquidity, finance important public projects, and help critical industries enduring economic hardship from regional oil trade disruptions.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), one trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $763 million) are redirected from existing Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) initiatives to bolster housing and construction development.

Al-Zaidi ordered that at least another one trillion Iraqi dinars ($763 million) be used to enhance the liquidity of the Trade Bank of Iraq (TBI) and the Industrial Bank to finance industrial and production-related investments.

An allocation of 500 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $382 million) is designated for the prompt settlement of longstanding governmental debts owed to private contractors and agricultural farmers.

A further investment of 500 billion Iraqi dinars (about $382 million) would bolster the national wealth fund, bringing its total balance to 1.5 trillion Iraqi dinars ($1,14 billion).

The domestic package incorporates structural measures aimed at fostering public-private partnerships, as the Iraqi government aims to strengthen its financial infrastructure following the end of the international coalition’s mission in the country.

World.title: Iraq’s Najaf receive first Iranian plane after US exemption
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Najaf International Airport in Iraq received the first Iranian flight from Tehran on Sunday, carrying over 150 passengers, marking the resumption of air travel between the two countries.

The Iraqi airport received the first flight arriving from Tehran operated by Iran’s Caspian Airlines with more than 150 passengers on board after a suspension that lasted over nine days.

The management of Najaf International Airport announced on Saturday that flights with Iran would resume on Sunday, with three evening flights scheduled, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

On Friday, Iraq announced that it had secured a sanctions waiver from Washington allowing Iranian airlines to operate dozens of daily flights to and from Najaf International Airport, with a similar exemption granted to Iraqi Airways.

Last week, all Iraqi airports began complying with the sanctions imposed by the United States on Iran’s entire aviation sector, causing significant disruptions at Najaf International Airport.

The Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement on Friday that an agreement had been reached allowing Iranian airlines, except Mahan Air, to operate 40 daily flights to and from Najaf International Airport.

The agreement follows efforts to facilitate the movement of travelers and visitors entering or leaving Iraq. It also aims to support humanitarian, medical, tourism, and educational initiatives.

World.title: Iraq plans to purchase large oil tankers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil has announced plans to secure funding for the purchase of new tankers—a move intended to bolster export operations and maximize revenues.

This initiative comes amid the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz and shipping disruptions in the Arabian Gulf. However, experts have raised questions regarding the project’s economic viability, cost, and timing, as well as its actual capacity to safeguard Iraqi exports during times of crisis.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Saturday that the ministry is coordinating with the government to secure the necessary funds to purchase oil tankers for the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC), enabling the firm to carry out crude oil transport operations.

Khudair noted that the ownership of such oil tankers would bolster exports, ensure economic viability, and maximize financial returns.

The IOTC once owned 23 tankers before its fleet dwindled over the past few decades due to wars, sanctions, and the suspension of modernization efforts.

Iraq’s current fleet is limited to six small-capacity tankers used primarily for transporting petroleum products and lacks supertankers for crude oil.

The Ministry of Oil is looking to acquire modern tankers with a capacity of two million barrels to enhance Iraq’s maritime transport capabilities and facilitate the transportation of a portion of its oil shipments.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament to discuss 2027 budget with $48.8 billion deficit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s parliament is about to start official deliberations on the 2027 federal budget, which has a significant 64 trillion Iraqi dinar ($48.8 billion) deficit.

Following the exclusion of a 2026 budget due to enormous political and economic challenges, the Iraqi Ministry of Finance has expedited the 2027 draft to meet the deadline for parliamentary submission.

The new budget’s total expenditure is projected at roughly 200 trillion Iraqi dinar (approximately $152.6 billion), matching previous record-high spending levels.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

Oil valuations in the new budget are based on a cautious benchmark price of $60 to $70 per barrel.

Earlier this year, regional military tensions prompted Iran to temporarily close the Strait of Hormuz, negatively affecting Iraqi oil exports.

At peak times of the crisis, Iraq’s monthly export volumes fell by almost 80 percent, resulting in tens of billions of dollars in lost income and a major public-sector salary issue.

Despite liquidity concerns, the Iraqi government is sustaining massive fixed expenses, including plans to permanently transfer almost one million contract workers and daily wage earners to permanent public service positions.

Additionally, tensions remain over allocations for the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG). According to reports, Erbil seeks a 14 percent share of the national budget based on recent census figures.

The Parliamentary Finance Committee is holding extensive preparatory briefings to look over non-oil income files, currency value, and social safety nets before the final document goes through its first reading.

World.title: German airlines to resume direct flights to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport revealed on Sunday that German airlines will resume direct flights to Baghdad International Airport, operating four weekly flights from Berlin and Dusseldorf.

The ministry said in a statement that Eurowings, a subsidiary of the Lufthansa Group, has announced that it will operate four direct weekly flights to Baghdad: two from Berlin and two from Dusseldorf.

The service, which is set to begin on December 10, 2026, reflects the growing confidence in Baghdad International Airport and the development of Iraq’s air transport sector.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to improve compliance with international criteria that apply to the national airline and Iraqi airports, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The development follows visits by specialized technical and operational delegations to Baghdad International Airport over the past three months to inspect the airport’s procedures and systems.

The visits ensured the airport’s compliance with international standards for security and operations, with the ultimate goal of meeting all flight operations requirements.

The decision represents a crucial advancement in enhancing the presence of European airlines within the Iraqi market.

The decision marks a big step toward increasing the operation of European airlines in the Iraqi market. It opens up new opportunities for European airlines to explore establishing more direct services to Baghdad.

German passenger airlines last flew to and from Iraq in the early 1980s. The new development signals the restoration of passenger services between the two countries. In addition, more than ten German companies have requested to operate flights to Iraq.

World.title: India tops Iraq U-17 Women 14–0 in Asian Cup qualifier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNew.com) – The Iraqi U-17 Women’s National Football Team endured a difficult opening fixture in the AFC U-17 Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers on Monday, October 5, 2026, falling 14–0 to India in their Group E curtain-raiser at the MP Selayang Stadium in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

The Indian side established early attacking dominance, concluding the first half with a commanding 7–0 advantage before adding another seven unanswered goals in the second period.

The encounter was disrupted in the 64th minute—with the scoreline standing at 9–0—when match officials enforced an extended weather stoppage due to heavy thunderstorms and lightning activity around the stadium perimeter before play resumed.

Despite the setback, the young Iraqi squad is preparing for two crucial remaining group fixtures as they continue their qualifying campaign:

Matchday 2: Facing tournament hosts Malaysia on Thursday, October 8, 2026, kicking off at 4:00 PM Baghdad Time.

Matchday 3: Concluding group play against Syria on Sunday, October 11, 2026, scheduled for an early morning kickoff at 10:30 AM Baghdad Time.

The coaching staff will focus on tactical adjustments and defensive organization to regroup the squad ahead of Thursday’s match against Malaysia.

World.title: Nujaba leader defies Baghdad arrests over US flag desecration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Akram Al-Kaabi, Secretary-General of Harakat al-Nujaba, voiced defiance against the Iraqi federal government following the arrest of several youths who desecrated the American flag during Sovereignty Day celebrations in Baghdad.

In a video published to his personal account on X (formerly Twitter), Al-Kaabi appeared walking across a U.S. flag spread on the ground, accompanied by the caption: “Your crimes are beneath our feet.”

The visual gesture followed a formal statement released by Harakat al-Nujaba on Sunday, October 4, demanding the immediate release of the detainees.

Abdul-Qadir Al-Karbalai, the movement’s military deputy, denounced the arrests in a post on X, characterizing the detention of demonstrators as a “dangerous precedent” that the group refused to tolerate.

The security crackdown originated during Sovereignty Day parades marking the full withdrawal of International Coalition forces from Iraq.

The Joint Operations Command confirmed the apprehension of individuals who trampled the American flag during a public procession in Baghdad, acting upon directives issued by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi.

The Prime Minister ordered the formation of a formal investigative committee to probe the incident and enforce legal standards governing public parades, coming as his administration pursues a comprehensive state monopoly over arms and works to balance foreign relations following the coalition’s departure.

World.title: US dollar surges past 160,000 IQD in Baghdad and Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar surged past the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency exchanges on Monday, October 5, 2026, marking a sharp escalation in exchange volatility and setting fresh multi-month highs across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

The rapid upward movement widens the spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s statutory official rate of 131,000 dinars per $100 to over 22.5 percent, reversing last week’s brief stabilization.

Daily market data showed that wholesale and retail exchange bureaus in Baghdad posted cash selling rates at 160,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 159,500 dinars, registering an increase of approximately 3,000 dinars compared to Thursday’s close.

In Erbil, the commercial capital of the Kurdistan Region, parallel desks quoted selling rates at 160,150 dinars per $100, while buying bids held at 159,750 dinars. In the southern trade center of Basra, greenbacks traded slightly lower but approached the barrier, with selling figures quoted at 159,500 dinars per $100 alongside buying offers at 159,000 dinars.

The sudden rally across domestic currency trading floors comes amid renewed cash-procurement pressure from private commercial merchants and wholesale importers securing foreign exchange outside the official electronic platform.

Currency traders in Baghdad note that heightened regional market friction and temporary lulls in physical greenback distribution have driven rapid retail speculation, pushing exchange rates past psychological resistance levels despite official regulatory efforts to anchor market liquidity.

World.title: Legislative privilege vs free speech: Supreme Court 7-judge bench may close case
World.content:
23-year legal duel (representative image)

NEW DELHI: Nearly 23 years after it stayed the arrests of some journalists following the Tamil Nadu assembly passing a breach of privilege resolution against them, the hearing scheduled before a seven-judge Supreme Court bench Wednesday, which promised to be a legal duel over the media's right to free speech versus the ambit of legislative privilege, appears to be an exercise for the records.For TN assembly, senior advocate Raju Ramachandran, flanked by attorney general R Venkataramani and solicitor general Tushar Mehta, told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the cause of action for the writ petition did not survive and the issue had become academic as the assembly withdrew the resolution imposing 15-day sentence on some journalists in 2004.A bench of CJI Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M Pancholi, Shree Chandrashekhar and V Mohana is scheduled to take up the petitions filed by N Ravi and S Selvam, then editors of 'The Hindu' and 'Murasoli' newspapers, respectively.Following the Nov 7, 2003, assembly resolution, arrest warrants were issued against the two editors and some journalists.CJI Kant said a seven-judge bench would assemble Tuesday, take the 2004 resolution on record and dispose of the petitions. Pendency in SC has increased to over 90,000 cases.

officials said Monday Form 6 had not been changed; only an additional declaration form had been introduced under the SIR documentation framework, to accompany it.

World.title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on sitting SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's criticism of deletion of a large number of voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) process, when the issue is pending adjudication before

, drew a sharp reaction from former CJI BR Gavai, who termed it judicial impropriety.

The former CJI refrained from directly commenting on his former colleague's remarks, but stressed a sitting or retired judge of Supreme Court, high court or any court must not speak on matters that are pending adjudication before a court.

"I am of the firm view that judicial discipline and propriety do not allow any sitting or retired judge to speak something which pertains to issues pending adjudication before SC, HC or any court," Justice Gavai said when asked by the media about Justice Bhuyan's statement at Nalsar, Hyderabad Sunday on the SIR of electoral rolls.

Besides Justice Bhuyan, former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman also criticised the intensive revision of rolls, saying a citizen's right to vote, which is at the heart of democracy, was at "great peril" because of "illegal knocking out" of people from voters' lists.

The SIR exercise in West Bengal was challenged before SC, which upheld it after tweaking the process by first engaging judicial officers in the scrutiny of documents and then providing for a special appeal provision by constituting tribunals.





However, petitions which challenge SIR in different states, where large-scale deletion of voters from draft rolls has taken place mainly because of "logical discrepancy" and "voter mapping" issues, are still pending in courts.

Justice Bhuyan, speaking at Nalsar, had said that any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens is intrinsically arbitrary as it strikes at the heart of the Constitution.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Former CJI Gavai said he does not want to comment on Justice Bhuyan's statement.

Justice Bhuyan had said, "Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens making them citizens without voting rights would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of the Constitution."

"If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary... No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution."

World.title: Probe sex assault case against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad, court directs Delhi cops
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has issued a notice to DCP, IGI airport, directing that an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad be completed and the report be filed by the next date of hearing, after rejecting

's request for more time.

The court of additional chief judicial magistrate Neha Mittal listed the matter for further hearing on Oct 23.

The complainant has accused Azad of raping her on the pretext of marriage.

Alleging that police failed to register an FIR, she had approached the court seeking a direction for registration of a case against Azad.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

During earlier proceedings, the court issued a notice to Delhi Police and asked for a status report.

Police submitted a status report detailing the progress of the inquiry conducted so far. However, they sought an additional two to three months to conclude the preliminary probe. The complainant opposed the police plea for more time.

The judge noted in the order that "since the offence alleged in the present application is punishable with life imprisonment, section 173(3) BNSS does not apply and hence, there is no scope for conducting preliminary inquiry".

Section 173(3) allows police to conduct a preliminary inquiry before registering an FIR for offences that carry a jail term of three to under seven years.

World.title: India, Switzerland eye deeper ties in trade, investment, tech
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and Switzerland looked to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, technology, defence production and nuclear energy as PM Modi held talks with visiting Swiss President Guy Parmelin.

The two countries also signed five agreements, including one for a migration and mobility partnership and another for exchange of young professionals.

Identifying innovation, infrastructure and advanced technology as strong pillars of the bilateral partnership, Modi said India and Switzerland were going to give the relationship a new momentum and take it to new heights.

The two countries set up a committee to facilitate trade and investment and address trade-related concerns, building upon Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) signed between India and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries in 2024.

TEPA was India's first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe, as Modi recalled.

"It is also an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity. Through this, we aim to achieve the targets of $100 billion in investment in India and 1 million direct jobs over the next 15 years," said Modi in his media statement.

Key highlights of TEPA included enhanced market access for Indian goods and services, $100 billion investment commitment over 15 years, creation of 1 million jobs in India and stronger bilateral relations with EFTA nations.





The leaders discussed the conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia, with the Swiss President welcoming Modi's message to Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war.

Modi said India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy and will continue to work together for global peace and stability.

"Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace," he said, adding that the leaders also agreed that reforms in global institutions are essential to address the growing global challenges.

PM said the mobility agreement will open up many new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals and young people. The agreement provides for multiple-entry visas for up to five years, including stays of up to six months on each visit, and renewable one-year student permits.

The two sides also signed another MoU to govern exchange of young professionals taking up temporary employment in the other country to enhance their professional and language skills.

According to the Indian govt, the MoU incorporates exchange of 300 persons annually per country, which may increase to 500, and a timeline of 30/90 days for verification of nationality/residency status, among other provisions.

Modi said both countries had taken several important decisions to increase market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries.

"This will help increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods to Switzerland. At the same time, we will attract Swiss investments into key sectors, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability," said Modi.

Parmelin said the partnership is mutually beneficial. "India gains from capital, technology transfers, and facilitated access to markets for high-value-added goods. Switzerland, for its part, benefits from exchanges with an immense partner experiencing sustained growth, at a time when global trade has become more exposed and unpredictable," said Parmelin.

World.title: Rajya Sabha polls: 8 fresh BJP faces for UP, Hardeep Puri among 2 ministers dropped
World.content:
Bengali film actor Koel Mallick with Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari after filing her nomination for the RS election in Kolkata

Whether BJP deploys Puri for Punjab polls remains to be seen

NEW DELHI: BJP on Monday did not renominate two Union ministers, Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, as its Rajya Sabha picks from Uttar Pradesh, rekindling speculation that PM Narendra Modi is looking to reshuffle his council of ministers as vacancies rise.Two other ministers, Ravneet Singh Bittu and George Kurien, were similarly left out of Rajya Sabha nominations in June, leading to their resignation. While these two were state ministers, a position held by Verma as well, Puri is a Cabinet minister holding the crucial portfolio of petroleum and natural gas.His likely exit from the Cabinet after the then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan quit in July following CJP's stir over paper leaks further makes the case of a reshuffle as both are demanding portfolios. Consumer affairs, food and public distribution minister Pralhad Joshi is currently handling the education ministry as an additional charge.A minister since Sep 2017, former diplomat Puri is the lone Sikh face in the council of ministers and had unsuccessfully contested the Lok Sabha election from Amritsar in 2019.Some Union ministers like Pankaj Chaudhary and Harsh Malhotra, now heading BJPâs state units in UP and Delhi respectively, have been given organisation responsibilities in an indication that their continuation in govt is unlikely to continue beyond the expected reshuffle.Puriâs term as Rajya Sabha MP from UP ends in Nov, and rules allow a minister to hold his office for six months without being an MP. Not having much of a political constituency of his own, it remains to be seen if he, like Bittu, will be deployed in the Punjab assembly polls, scheduled to be held along with four other states, including UP, early next year.While the impending Punjab election was cited by some experts as a case for his continuation due to his Sikh background, BJP brass in the end chose to not repeat any of its RS candidates, a practice it had followed in the last round of elections as well.Since taking over as PM in 2014, Modi has gone for an overhaul of his council of ministers before the mid-term in both his earlier stints, giving rise to the prospect of a major rejig as his govt is now well into its third year in its third stint.

World.title: SIR row: Will annul Election Commission orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday asked the

, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to clarify whether crucial decisions regarding the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls were taken unilaterally by the CEC, and said it would injunct (bar) those decisions by the three-member commission which were neither unanimous nor by majority.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said irrespective of powers vested in the CEC, the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. âIf we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,â it said.

The statement came after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, strongly argued for an interim direction to the EC to only take decisions by unanimity during pendency of the petition as the amended CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, gave the CEC enormous powers.

The PIL has sought scrutiny of the validity of SIR decisions and âalterationsâ in Form 6 for new voters. Singh said since the court could not undo elections, a direction must be issued that in the interregnum, EC must follow the statutory mandate. He pleaded that EC be directed to preserve all records on SIR decisions and Form 6 alteration and produce them before SC for scrutiny.

CEC, ECs need to either rebut or endorse allegations about âunilateral decisionsâ

Let us have some authenticated facts before us through their responses.





They must respond in a clear and transparent manner. If the records show some of the decisions are not taken by majority, we will injunct those. But we cannot put the cart before the horse, the bench said while also issuing notices to the Centre, deputy EC Manish Garg and ECâs director general (IT) Seema Khanna.

This has set the stage for the CEC and, more crucially, the two ECs to either endorse or rebut the allegation that important decisions on SIR were taken by Gyanesh Kumar unilaterally and in violation of the law which lays down that the commissionâs calls are to be made either unanimously or, failing that, by majority.

The allegation, based on a newspaper report, is at the core of the controversy which has reignited opposition to SIR.

Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, also questioned the validity of Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provided that âno court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is, or was, a CEC or an election commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or functionâ.

He said this was way beyond the immunity enjoyed even by SC judges and especially when it was not extended even to the PM.

Justice Bagchi said, âWe will examine the expression âor wasâ. Protection while in office is understandable. Such protection (as provided under Section 16) is perhaps only with regard to the President. It is not given to constitutional court judges under Judges Inquiry Act.â

Singh pleaded for suspension of the CEC or divesting him of his authority.

When the bench asked who would conduct elections, Singh said the other two ECs would do it. He said in the interim, the SC-mandated selection panel for CEC should be brought back in which the CJI is included along with the PM and the LoP. The 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union minister nominated by the PM.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

When the bench declined, Singh said the situation was so grave that it could undermine the very basis of our democracy.

âToday, the CEC is acting in a manner which is contrary to the statute under which he is appointed. Court should pass some interim orders (restraining the CEC from discharging his functions), otherwise the country will burn,â he said.

Patna-based petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh has sought a direction to EC to âproduce before SC the complete original and primary records relating to the matters pleaded herein, including minutes, agendas, approvals, file notings, work allocation and delegation orders, IT-access records, server logs, audit trails and database-change histories concerning the functioning of the commission, ERONet/EClNet, alteration of Form 6 and filing of appeals before the Bengal appellate tribunalsâ.

World.title: National Commission for Women issues safety guidelines to step-up monitoring of app-based and digital transport services
World.content:
The NCW issued guidelines for the safety of women using app-based cabs (representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking note of safety concerns emerging from across states the National Commission for Women has issued guidelines to states and UTs for safety of women passengers using app-based and digital transport services calling for appropriate verification of criminal antecedents, police verification and background of drivers before onboarding, monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours and providing SOS buttons in every cab to send out alerts to the command-and-control centre.The NCW notes that as cabs, auto-rickshaws, bike taxis and other app-enabled transport services have become an integral part of everyday mobility, particularly for women travelling independently, ensuring safety throughout the journey has assumed greater importance.Instances relating to mismatch in driver or vehicle identity, route deviation, inappropriate conduct, harassment, stalking, unsafe drop-offs, delays in emergency response and inadequate grievance redressal underline the need for a coordinated and accountable safety framework.The guidelines issued in this backdrop also take into consideration the recommendations of the Justice J S Verma Committee Report, 2013, and the regulatory framework under the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, issued by the ministry of road transport and highways.NCW chairperosn Vijaya Rahatkar, has written to the chief secretaries of all states and UTs, requesting appropriate measures for implementation of the guidelines.Bringing focus on verification of driver and vehicle, the guidelines lay down that the aggregators shall ensure that the driver and vehicle assigned to a passenger match the details displayed on the application. âAny unauthorised change in the driver or vehicle shall be appropriately flagged in the application and treated as a safety concern,â it asserts. The guidelines also call for mechanisms for real-time alerts for route deviations or suspicious stoppages.The guidelines also call for penalty-free cancellation in case of identity mismatch. The guidelines also lay down that the aggregators must strive to maintain a verified pool of women drivers, enabling women travelling alone with the option to request a woman driver through the application.Calling for enhanced verification and monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours, the guidelines set out measures ranging from mandatory driver photo verification at trip commencement, addressing driver intoxication, enhanced command and control centre monitoring and a safe-drop option at the end of the ride.âAggregators may establish a dedicated and time-bound grievance redressal mechanism for complaints relating to driver misconduct, harassment, assault, route deviation, unauthorised driver or vehicle substitution and failure of emergency-response mechanisms,â the guidelines state.

World.title: Shinde meets PM Modi over Maharashtra drought, says Centre assures support for farmers
World.content:
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Monday (October 5, 2026) and discussed the drought situation in Maharashtra, with Mr. Shinde saying the Centre had assured the State of support for farmers affected by the crisis.

The hour-long meeting focused on the situation facing farmers, including water availability, agricultural conditions and the availability of fodder for livestock, according to a statement issued by Mr. Shinde’s office.

Mr. Shinde said Mr. Modi sought details about the situation in Maharashtra and assured him that the Centre would extend necessary assistance. He expressed confidence that Maharashtra would receive substantial support considering the scale of the crisis.

“Farmers’ Diwali will not be marred by the drought crisis,” Mr. Shinde said, adding that the State government would stand firmly behind farmers during the difficult period.

Mr. Shinde said farmers currently receive ₹12,000 annually through financial assistance provided jointly by the Centre and the Maharashtra government. This includes ₹6,000 under the Centre’s farmer assistance scheme and another ₹6,000 through the State government’s Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana.

Referring to assistance extended to farmers following heavy rains last year, Mr. Shinde said the government would not hesitate to provide support when the agricultural community was facing distress.

“The farming community has the first right over the government treasury. When farmers are in distress, the government will not hold back assistance,” he said.

Mr. Shinde also criticised the Opposition, accusing it of focusing on marches, protests and allegations against Mr. Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah instead of raising substantive issues concerning the public.

The Deputy Chief Minister also spoke about the upcoming Legislative Council elections. He said the Mahayuti coordination committee had discussed Mangesh Chivte’s candidature from the Pune Teachers’ Constituency.

Mr. Shinde said his party had issued the AB Form to Mr. Chivte and that he would file his nomination on Tuesday (October 6, 2026).

Responding to a question on a possible Cabinet expansion, Mr. Shinde said Mr. Modi, as the principal leader of the National Democratic Alliance, would take an appropriate decision on the matter at the right time.

World.title: Supreme Court quashes Bombay HC order directing Maharashtra FDA to pay ₹5 lakh compensation
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) set aside a Bombay High Court direction ordering the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to pay ₹5 lakh compensation to a Pune-based dairy and sweets establishment whose food licence had been suspended following a food poisoning complaint.

The order was passed in State of Maharashtra & Ors. v. M/s Gurunanak Dairy & Sweets on October 5, according to a press note issued by the Maharashtra FDA.

The case dates back to June 12, when FDA food safety officers in Pune inspected the establishment following a complaint of food poisoning. Officials found deficiencies relating to hygiene, maintenance of records, labelling, and the personal hygiene of employees, following which its food licence was suspended under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

According to the FDA, a sample of "Malai Pedha" collected from the establishment during the inspection was subsequently declared unsafe. The State argued before the Supreme Court that the suspension was therefore undertaken in the interest of public health and in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act.

The proprietor challenged the suspension by filing a statutory appeal before the Commissioner, FDA, on June 15. The establishment subsequently submitted a compliance report on July 9, following which the FDA carried out a reinspection on July 13, four days after receiving the report.

The establishment later approached the Bombay High Court through Writ Petition No. 9905 of 2026. On August 17, the High Court revoked the suspension of its food licence and directed the FDA to deposit ₹5 lakh as compensation for business losses suffered by the establishment.

The Maharashtra government challenged the compensation direction before the Supreme Court. It argued that the FDA had acted promptly at every stage and that the establishment's statutory appeal before the FDA Commissioner was pending and had been reserved for a decision.

The State further maintained that the FDA's actions were neither malicious nor arbitrary and that there had been no deliberate delay. It argued that time taken in good faith during a statutory process could not form the basis for imposing a financial penalty or compensation on the government.

Accepting the State's submissions, the Supreme Court set aside the Bombay High Court's direction requiring the FDA to pay ₹5 lakh and quashed the compensation order, according to the press note.

World.title: First international cargo vessel leaves eastern Assam since 1947
World.content:
A barge carrying 540 metric tonnes of methanol left the Bogibeel Terminal in Dibrugarh district for Dhaka, Bangladesh, on Monday (October 5, 2025), marking the first international shipment from eastern Assam since India’s independence in 1947.

Sarbananda Sonowal, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, flagged off the vessel DLB Patkai, pushed by the tug Kushal Konwar, carrying methanol produced by the State-owned Assam Petrochemicals Limited in Namrup.

The vessel, destined for Pangaon port in Dhaka’s Narayanganj, will travel about 768 km down the Brahmaputra River (National Waterway-2) to the India-Bangladesh border, and continue along the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route in the neighbouring country. The total distance is about 1,300 km.

Mr. Sonowal said the cargo shipment is seen as a test of whether the Brahmaputra can serve as a commercially viable freight corridor linking the northeastern region to overseas markets.

“Our grandparents grew up hearing the steamer whistle at Dibrugarh ghat. For 70 years, that whistle fell silent, and the ships stopped coming. A cargo vessel has left Dibrugarh for the world once again. The river never failed us, but the will to revive the route was lacking for decades,” he said.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who attended the flagging-off virtually, said the revival of international cargo movement was a “proud day for Assam”.

Inland Waterways Authority of India officials said the shipment became possible after Customs and Immigration complexes were recently set up at Bogibeel and Dhubri. Dhubri, on India’s border with Bangladesh, is metaphorically where the Brahmaputra blends into the Jamuna in the neighbouring country.

Busy past

Dibrugarh was once among the busiest river ports in eastern India. Government-run steamers reached the town from Calcutta, now Kolkata, by 1856.

In 1882, the Dibru-Sadiya Railway began operating from the Dibrugarh ghat. By 1913, steamers sailed up the Brahmaputra to the town daily, carrying tea, timber and passengers.

The 1947 Partition cut that route, forcing Assam’s goods to pass through the then East Pakistan to reach Calcutta. A 1950 earthquake disturbed the riverbed at Dibrugarh, and regular bookings from Dibrugarh ghat stopped in 1954.

The Dibrugarh ghat closed on October 15, 1956, as western ports on the Brahmaputra — Dhubri and Pandu in Guwahati — continued to handle international cargo occasionally.

The 1965 war between India and Pakistan suspended cross-border river trade. India and Bangladesh signed a river trade protocol in 1972.

In 1988, the 891 km stretch of the Brahmaputra from Sadiya to Dhubri was declared National Waterway 2. Regular cargo service on the waterway resumed in December 2017, when cement moved from Pandu to Dhubri.

According to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, cargo on India’s national waterways rose from 18 million metric tonnes in fiscal 2013-14 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26.

More than ₹68 billion (about $770 million) is being invested in waterways across the northeast, including the development of National Waterway-2, a ship repair facility at Pandu and last-mile connectivity to Pandu port, Mr. Sonowal said.

“Every tonne we move on the river means less fuel burnt and fewer trucks on the highway,” he said, adding that India is working with Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, and Myanmar on regional waterway links.

World.title: Set to leave party, NC MP Ruhullah meets students at Kashmir University, calls for ‘restoring students’ voice’
World.content:
Rebel National Conference (NC) Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah, who has threatened to leave the party in November this year, on Monday (October 5, 2026) met students at Kashmir University (KU), where the authorities have barred on-campus students’ politics since 2019.

“One concern was raised by almost everyone that students have no representation. Whether it’s an academic, hostel or administrative issue, there is no students’ union to take it up. A university without a student voice is incomplete. Students deserve a seat at the table,” said MP Ruhullah, after an unannounced tour of the campus.

Mr. Ruhullah said he spent time with the students on campus in Srinagar’s Hazratbal area. “The discussion covered the reservation policy, student activism, the role of students in active politics and the current state of education in J&K,” said MP Ruhullah.

The rebel NC MP has started an outreach in J&K ahead of the proposed resignation on November 3 this year from the party. He has repeatedly expressed unhappiness over the party’s failure to work towards its manifesto, which calls for restoration of special status under Article 370 to J&K.

Mr. Ruhullah’s decision to quit the party comes amid growing differences with J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, whom he has publicly criticised. The reason behind choosing November 3 to quit the party is that Mr. Ruhullah’s father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was a popular cleric, was assassinated by militants in a powerful Improvised Explosive Device (IED) blast in north Kashmir’s Magam road on November 3, 2000.

World.title: Woman journalist who accused ACP of sexual harassment during protest among 17 booked by Delhi Police; all granted conditional bail
World.content:
The Delhi Police on Monday (October 5, 2026) registered an FIR against a woman journalist who has accused Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat of sexual harassment and manhandling, along with 16 other protesters, shortly after they were detained for staging a protest Parliament Street police station demanding registration of a case against the officer.

The Delhi government, meanwhile, clarified that the October 5 order assigning current duty charge of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police to 12 DANIPS officers was based on a proposal initiated on August 25, well before the present allegations. Earlier in the day, the accused official, an Assistant Commissioner of police rank officer, was promoted to the rank of Additional Deputy Commissioner of police on Monday in an order signed by the Deputy Secretary (Home) Ramesh Kumar.

Later, a Government order stated that the assignment was a temporary arrangement carrying no financial benefit and did not confer the statutory powers of a regular incumbent. ACP Vivek Bhagat subsequently requested that he not be given the current duty charge until a full enquiry into the allegations of harassment of women journalists was completed. The order has been modified accordingly, with the charge to be assigned to the remaining 11 officers.

The FIR was registered by the Parliament Street police station after the protesters had spent a second consecutive night outside the station demanding registration of a case against ACP Bhagat. The 17 protesters were detained on Monday (October 5, 2026) morning and initially taken to the Delhi Cantonment police station before being taken to different police stations in the New Delhi district.

Later in the night, following a brief period of arrest, all 17 protesters were granted conditional bail.

Court directs report on custodial torture allegations

A Patiala House court granted bail to all 17 accused in the case, observing that although the allegations against them were “serious in nature”, all the offences invoked against them, except Sections 132 and 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, were bailable. The court noted that Section 132, which relates to assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharge of duty, carries a maximum punishment of two years, as per the bail order seen by The Hindu. It also noted that the accused were young and did not appear to be habitual offenders.

The court, however, also took note of allegations of custodial assault made by two of the accused. According to the order, accused Dharmender and Samarth alleged that they had been beaten inside Parliament Street police station after being detained, while Sheikh Yunus alleged that he was injured after being pushed during the protest. The court noted that medical reports recorded abrasions, tenderness, contusions and swelling in some of the accused. It directed that a report be called from the DCP, New Delhi, regarding the allegations of custodial torture and ordered that relevant CCTV footage from Parliament Street police station be preserved.

The police, in opposing bail, alleged that the protesters had formed an unlawful assembly despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, obstructed public space, manhandled police personnel, including a woman officer, and assaulted them, resulting in injuries to one officer. The police also alleged that the protesters broke the window and rear-side glass of the bus in which they were being taken, causing damage to public property. These allegations were recorded by the court as the investigating officer’s submissions and were not findings of guilt.

While granting bail, the court said that a person has a right to protest peacefully, but assaulting police officials on duty cannot be permitted under the garb of a peaceful protest. At the same time, it held that, considering the nature of the offences, the young age of the accused and the fact that they did not appear to be habitual offenders, there was no justification for keeping them in judicial custody. The accused were granted bail on a bond of ₹15,000 each with one surety of a like amount, subject to conditions including not tampering with evidence or influencing witnesses and appearing before the court on each date of hearing.

The two women journalists were released from Mandir Marg police station on Monday evening, while the remaining 15 protesters were released later.

This comes at a time when the woman journalist had been seeking an FIR against ACP Vivek Bhagat after alleging that he sexually harassed and shoved her while she was covering a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 3. She has said the alleged incident occurred while she was recording the detention of All India Students’ Association president Neha Bora.

She had also been detained during the October 4 protest and was detained again on Monday (October 5, 2026) morning.

The Crime Branch, to which three complaints alleging sexual harassment and manhandling by police personnel were transferred on Sunday (October 4, 2026), had not registered an FIR in any of the cases by Monday (October 5, 2026) evening, nearly 48 hours after the alleged incidents.

On Sunday (October 4, 2026), the Delhi Police said three women journalists had submitted complaints alleging sexual harassment and manhandling by police officers during the October 3 protest. The complaints were transferred to the Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial enquiry”.

The complainant had spent several hours at the Parliament Street police station on Sunday (October 4, 2026) seeking registration of an FIR.

The police have maintained that the concerned personnel were performing law and order duties during the protest. An official told The Hindu that registering cases against police personnel for actions taken in the course of such duties could “deter them from working”.

A New Delhi police official had also told The Hindu on Sunday (October 4, 2026) that there was no evidence to substantiate the allegation and that footage from the many cameras present at the protest should establish whether the incident had occurred.

The developments have drawn political and civil society reactions. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, in a post on X, alleged that women protesters and journalists had been subjected to mistreatment by the Delhi Police during the recent protests and questioned the absence of an FIR on the journalist’s complaint.

“What’s happening in Delhi right now follows a single pattern: silence any woman who dares to ask questions,” Mr. Gandhi said, alleging that female protesters had complained of misbehaviour by male police officers and that cameras had been snatched from women journalists.

He also referred to recent accounts by journalists Shaheen and Nafisa of alleged violence and mistreatment inside the Saket police station and demanded that CCTV footage from the station be made public and action be taken against police personnel found guilty.

Legal affairs head of the Cockroach Janta Party Ratna Singh alleged that the detainees were assaulted and “brutally beaten” by the police.

Advocate Supantha Sinha of the Association for Indian Labour and Administrative Justice (AILAJ), who was on the ground to coordinate the legal response, alleged that the detainees were assaulted during their detention and subsequently taken to Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital for medical examination and medico-legal certificates.

The continuing protests have also brought wider complaints from women protesters about their treatment during the demonstrations from October 2. Several women, including students, have alleged sexual harassment and manhandling by police personnel during their detention.

World.title: 19,000 West Bengal voters to miss bypolls as appeals remain pending in tribunals
World.content:
Nearly 19,000 voters in West Bengal’s Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly constituencies, where byelections are being held on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), are among the 38.31 lakh voters in West Bengal who remain disenfranchised due to the crawling pace of work at the Appellate Tribunals where their cases are pending. The Calcutta High Court had in July observed that at the current rate, it would take 21 years for the tribunals to clear the cases.

In Rejinagar, the total number of appeals submitted was 12,452, out of which four have been included so far, and in Nandigram, the total number of appeals submitted was 6,443, with 89 included so far. While in both places, no one has been excluded so far, the tribunals have, till now, cleared only 1.26 lakh of the total 38.31 lakh appeals, which is approximately 3% of the total cases.

Out of the 19 Appellate Tribunals set up by the Election Commission (ECI) in March, only 16 remain functional, as three retired judges — Justice T.S. Sivagnanam, Justice Ranjit Bag and Justice Indrajit Chatterjee — have quit, citing various functional issues. Their positions remain vacant.

The ECI’s proposal to increase the number of tribunals from 19 to 42 has also not moved forward. The Supreme Court was scheduled to hear the matter on Monday (October 5), but it was not listed.

The poll body’s special “door-to-door” drive to re-enrol any voter left behind during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process through Form 6, announced last week, will also not be applicable to them.

The Appellate Tribunals came out of the Supreme Court’s supervision of the SIR. Judicial officers, drawn from a list the Calcutta High Court sent at the Supreme Court’s direction, were adjudicating the roughly 60 lakh “doubtful and pending” cases. On March 10, the top court had directed that a separate appellate body be set up so that people could challenge those officers’ decisions.

Of the roughly 60 lakh “doubtful” cases, the 700 judicial officers cleared and restored approximately 32.77 lakh (32,77,360) voters onto the electoral rolls. The remaining 27.23 lakh were rejected, of whom 22 lakh appealed to the tribunals.

The ECI constituted the Appellate Tribunals for West Bengal on March 21. The tribunals began functioning around April 13, and on April 16, the Supreme Court ordered that voters whose appeals succeed be added through a supplementary list. The verdict came only days before Assembly elections began on April 23, and reportedly only 136 names had been cleared by then.

Parallelly, 16,10,311 bulk appeals were instituted at the Appellate Tribunals challenging the decision to include voters restored by the judicial officers, bringing the total number of cases pending in the tribunals to a little more than 38 lakh.

World.title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar has lost public trust and must be removed, say former bureaucrats, activists
World.content:
A group of senior retired bureaucrats, civil society activists, and academics accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of six instances of “proved misbehaviour” and sought his removal, but could not submit their “notice of impeachment” to him in person, as heavy barricading and police deployment prevented the delegation from reaching the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) office on Mondy (October 5, 2026).

They subsequently emailed their “chargesheet” to the CEC. It invokes Article 324(5) of the Constitution, which protects the CEC from removal except on grounds of “proved misbehaviour or incapacity”, and alleges that the CEC’s conduct amounted to a sustained disregard of law and constitutional duty.

The 14-member delegation included former Delhi Lieutenant-Governor Najeeb Jung, former Union Home Secretary G.K. Pillai, and other former IAS officers and ambassadors.

‘People’s impeachment notice’

The chargesheet lists six accusations against Mr. Kumar, including that he undermined the collective functioning of the ECI, made unauthorised changes to the statutory Form 6, centralised electoral-roll functions through the ECINET platform, and presided over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls that the activists alleged has resulted in large-scale disenfranchisement.

The group said the charges amounted to a “people’s impeachment” of the CEC and argued that he had lost the public trust necessary to continue in office. “EC is functioning illegally and failing in its responsibility. We believe that the CEC must resign,” activist Anjali Bhardwaj said.

The group alleged that the CEC had weakened the Commission’s collective decision-making, introduced changes to Form 6 that placed an additional burden on voters seeking inclusion in the rolls, and used technological systems in ways that encroached on the statutory functions of Electoral Registration Officers. The chargesheet alleges that the conduct of the Commission during the SIR had compromised citizens’ ability to establish their eligibility for inclusion in the electoral rolls, adding that such conduct undermined the Commission’s independence and public credibility.

‘No moral authority’

“It is losing the trust. CEC Gyanesh Kumar has no moral authority to stay in office. First [it] defended [the changes], saying changes to Form 6 have been upheld by the Supreme Court but the court denied that today. How do people trust the Commission?” Ms. Bhardwaj said.

The delegation listed in the chargesheet comprises former Delhi Lieutenant-Governor Najeeb Jung, former Union Home Secretary G.K. Pillai, former Union Secretary Amitabha Pande, retired IAS officer Jayashree Mukherjee, former Ambassador Ashok Sharma, former Special Director of the Intelligence Bureau and Central Information Commissioner Yashovardhan Azad, former civil servant Ashish Joshi, student activist Aishe Ghosh, N. Sai Balaji, Dinesh Srirangarajan, Sandeep Yadav, Amrita Johri, Yogendra Yadav, and Ms. Bhardwaj.

“Since we could not reach there, we emailed them the chargesheet,” Ms. Bhardwaj said. “We first planned to meet at the Constitution Club and then go to the Nirvachan Bhawan [the Commission building] from there. But we couldn’t reach there because of barricading. Then we met at the Press Club and decided to go from there, and we got to know Election Commission itself is heavily barricaded and police deployment is there. Whichever roads we were taking were barricaded,” she added.

World.title: Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 ‘illegally’ during SIR, says Rahul Gandhi
World.content:
Mounting an offensive against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Congress on Monday (October 5, 2026) accused the CEC of “lying” after the Supreme Court said it had not approved of any changes to Form 6 during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in various States.

Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: Follow LIVE updates on October 5, 2026

Form 6 is an application through which, an eligible person seeks inclusion in the electoral roll for the first time.

The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, on his X handle, shared a screenshot of the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) statement on September 26, 2026, which read: “The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used.”

“It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP. He and everyone else involved in this criminal assault on our democracy will be held accountable,” Mr. Gandhi said.

The Opposition leader’s remarks came after the Supreme Court issued notices to the ECI and the Centre on a petition that alleged the poll body took several decisions without the approval of the two Election Commissioners.

In a separate post on X, Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge said resignation of the CEC, annulling the SIR and conducting elections on ballot papers are “non-negotiable demands” of the principal Opposition party.

Mr. Kharge said Congress workers and INDIA bloc partners are on the streets over these three issues across the country. He said the Congress stands in solidarity with civil society members and youth organisations that are struggling on these issues in various places across the country.

“The dictator is extremely panicked; get ready for another chapter in the distraction tactics,” the Congress chief said, adding, “The Congress Party’s 3 demands are non-negotiable. First, the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar. Second, the annulment of SIR. Third, conducting elections on Ballot Paper”.

Taking note of the Supreme Court’s notices to the ECI and the Centre and the top court’s observation that it will annul decisions found not to be in accordance with law, Congress communication chief Jairam Ramesh said the Supreme Court has a remarkable opportunity to restore public confidence in the ECI.

He accused the CEC of “betraying” the Constitution in letter and spirit at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

“Based on the recent damning revelations regarding (1) the ad-hoc, illegal and slip-shod manner in which the SIR was taking place, (2) criticism from both sitting and retired Judges of the Supreme Court, (3) the vast and indiscriminate (and many obviously incorrect) deletions without adequate due process, the Supreme Court has a remarkable opportunity to restore public confidence in an institution vital to the integrity of our republic,” Mr. Ramesh said on X.

“Obviously and very clearly the CEC lied. Form 6 was deliberately modified by the CEC himself to delete Gen Z voters of whom the PM is simply terrified,” Mr. Ramesh said in another post.

World.title: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday following an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh.

The three countries held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, the FO statement said.

“The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” it added.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict.

In the Riyadh meeting, the three members of the Makkah Defence Alliance condemned “in the strongest terms” the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madina, as well as the continuing attacks targeting cities and civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their “unequivocal rejection of any attack or threat against the kingdom’s security and territorial integrity”, the statement said.

For their part, Pakistan and Turkiye commended the “vigilance and readiness of the Saudi armed forces, as well as the professionalism and high level of competence they have demonstrated in countering the threats and attacks facing the kingdom and in safeguarding its security and territorial integrity”, the FO said.

The SPDC reviewed the outcomes of the political and military consultations preceding the meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it, affirming that the Makkah pact embodied a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats, it said.

Moreover, the three countries affirmed that the security of each member of the alliance was an “integral part of the collective security of the three countries, and that translating the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence into practical measures demonstrates the credibility of the commitment to collective defence, strengthens the effectiveness of deterrence, and reaffirms the unity and determination of our three countries to defend their security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, in accordance with the provisions of the agreement”.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis.

When asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

“Whatever assistance they require is being provided. But right now, the Turkish and Pakistani armies are playing a supportive role,” he said, noting that Pakistan was involved in reconnaissance.

The defence minister said the meeting was primarily focused on formalising the Makkah alliance’s operational structure.

“The organisational structure of the alliance was formalised during today’s meeting,” he said.

As part of the institutional development of the Makkah alliance, the SPDC decided to appoint Pakistan’s Lieutenant General (Retd) Nauman Mahmood as the first secretary general of the alliance for a three-year term, the FO statement said.

“The parties welcomed him, wished him every success in the discharge of his duties, and expressed their confidence in his contribution to advancing the alliance and achieving its objectives,” it added.

In an earlier statement on social media platform X, the FO said Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) included Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Asif.

“The meeting will also be attended by the respective ministers of foreign affairs, ministers of defence, as well as chiefs of general staff of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and the Republic of Türkiye,” the FO added.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The SPDC meeting under it has been held as Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition government launched a major military campaign on Sunday to recapture territory held by the Houthis.

Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis showed no signs of abating over the weekend, with the Houthis saying the kingdom had launched dozens of strikes on Yemen’s capital Sanaa, after which they attacked an Aramco facility with ballistic missiles and drones south of Riyadh.

The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait in a lightning offensive.

On Sept 25, the military chiefs of Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh for urgently convened talks under the pact in light of the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

On Sept 18, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry had expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying Pakistan will go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

World.title: After breakdown of talks with govt, PTI says reconciliation not possible without including Imran
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PTI leaders on Monday declared that reconciliation between their party and the government was not possible without including incarcerated party founder Imran Khan in the dialogue process.

Narrating the opposition’s stance on why the talks with the government failed over the weekend, PTI’s secretary general, Salman Akram Raja, presented his party’s demand that Imran be included in any future political dialogue.

“Only [Imran] has the capability to bridge the gulf that has developed between the state and the nation,” Raja said during the press conference held at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa House in Islamabad.

“Imran Khan is very important for us and we had every right to seek his opinion, but it was not allowed,” Raja said.

The PTI leader said that another reason for the failure of the talks was that the government was not willing to pursue a collective strategy against terrorism. Raja told the media that the PTI had entered into the negotiations with sincerity and was serious about addressing the issues.

“Even on the second day, we were hoping that another round of talks would streamline things,” he said.

Describing the reasons for talks failing, Raja said: “We were being pushed to support the government over every action being taken regarding terrorism in KP.”

He added that the PTI had demanded that the government respect the recommendations and opinions of a jirga held by the KP Assembly, in which political parties and stakeholders had participated.

The jirga had recommended solutions to the problem, the opposition delegation had told the government, according to Raja.

The delegation had also asked the government to consider the opinions of tribal leaders, Raja said.

He said the PTI had suggested the agreement should mention that a collective decision would be made regarding terrorism, but the government had said it would not put it down on paper.

“We were told that a unanimous strategy against terrorism would not be developed and it would not be included in the agreement,” he said. Raja said that the government had deliberately complicated the situation.

“It is a fact that the current issues can only be addressed by Imran Khan.

“We had demanded that Imran Khan and his opinion should be included in all issues, which is why we demanded a meeting of party leaders with him,” Raja said.

The two rounds of talks between the government and the opposition held on Friday and Saturday did not yield positive results, with counterterrorism policies and access to Imran emerging as two major sticking points.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who was part of the process, on Sunday singled out KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi for the failure of talks, saying that he changed the agreement.

Separately, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the PTI representatives came for talks but were unwilling to abandon their “double standards and hypocrisy”.

For its part, the PTI said it wanted immediate access to party founder Imran for consultations, and even agreed to forgo other demands for this. However, the government declined to make access to Imran part of the proposed agreement, the opposition party claimed.

Addressing the failed talks, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam said on Monday that the government’s delegation had suggested that both sides “be on the same page” about terrorism.

Following the failed talks, the PTI went ahead with its protest march on Sunday despite warnings from the federal government.

KP Assembly speaker to summon security committee meeting

Against this backdrop, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Swati said he was going to summon another meeting of a special committee on security, which was constituted after a peace jirga in the assembly in November last year.

“I am again summoning a meeting of the special committee. I wish for the relevant authorities and institutions to sit together on this important matter,” he posted on X.

He emphasised that it was important to consider this process initiated by the KP Assembly before the Centre held the former responsible for the law and order situation in the province.

Swati recalled that political parties had issued a joint statement after the Nov peace jirga, in light of which the assembly had constituted a special committee on security. The committee, he said, was briefed by the provincial police chief, the Counterterrorism Department, the KP home additional chief secretary, the Home Department, the KP chief secretary and other relevant provincial institutions.

“We also informed the leadership in the Centre about this process and sent letters to the prime minister, the Senate chairman, the National Assembly speaker and the interior minister, informing them that the assembly was moving towards [formulating] comprehensive parliamentary recommendations,” he said.

Swati said just one important official, the Peshawar corps commander, was left to brief the committee.

“I had spoken to the Peshawar corps commander and he had assured me of his participation. However, the meeting has yet to take place,” he added.

“I am again summoning a meeting of the special committee. I wish for the relevant authorities and institutions to sit together on this important matter.

“Whatever we have heard, seen, and whatever facts have come before the committee — they will present their stance; the relevant institutions will present theirs,” Swati said.

Following that, he continued, the committee would formulate its recommendations, which would be presented before the assembly.

“After the assembly’s approval, the recommendations will be forwarded to the provincial and federal governments so that responsibility, policy and practical measures are clearly [stated].”

The speaker said the people of KP wanted peace and called for the relevant parties to play their respective roles in moving towards a collective solution.

“We have to find a way while collectively implementing the National Action Plan, clarifying the responsibilities of relevant institutions,” he added.

Later, it emerged that Swati had sent a letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging the implementation of the joint declaration issued by the assembly’s peace jirga in 2025.

In the letter, a copy of which is available with Dawn, Swati noted that a special committee on security had been constituted in the province to prepare a comprehensive report on the security situation after “due consultation with all relevant stakeholders”. This committee actively sought engagement with the KP governor, the provincial government, political leadership, elected representatives, the Armed Forces, and other relevant security institutions regarding the law and order situation in the province.

A peace jirga was held on Nov 12 last year in continuation of this process, Swati added, which was attended by over 30 leading members of political parties, elected representatives and other stakeholders.

“After detailed deliberations, the jirga adopted a joint declaration reflecting the collective concerns and aspirations of the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, particularly with regard to terrorism, security, and the restoration of lasting peace,” the letter stated, adding that this declaration had already been shared with the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) for consideration.

Swati’s letter further noted that the committee also received detailed briefings from provincial government departments and institutions about “the prevailing security situation, the nature of threats confronting the province, and the measures being undertaken to address them”.

It clarified that the committee’s objective in seeking such insight was not to interfere in the operational responsibilities of security agencies, but rather to keep elected representatives fully informed on matters that affected their constituents.

“The special committee has prepared a report on the security situation in the light of these briefings,” Swati said, noting that this was intended to be forwarded to the federal government for inclusion in the National Action Plan as well as to the KP government as part of effective counter-terrorism measures.

However, he added, the report could not be finalised as the Corps Commander, XI Corps was not available to provide a briefing. The letter noted that the committee remained engaged with his office and other stakeholders in order to finalise the report.

Once finalised, the report will be placed before the KP Assembly for adoption and shared with all stakeholders as a guiding policy document.

The speaker affirmed the provincial assembly’s readiness to fully cooperate with the federal government in efforts to curb terrorism “through the building of public opinion, owned and led by the public representatives”.

He expressed his confidence that the premier would consider the matter and extend “every possible support” towards building a national consensus for lasting peace in KP.

World.title: PTI long march: KP CM's convoy halts in Kohat for the night, heads for Peshawar on Tuesday
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday resumed PTI’s march, leading a convoy from from Karak to Kohat where the protesters will spend the night.

The opposition has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the Centre, which has vowed to prevent any gatherings in Islamabad. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan.

PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons, particularly over the counterterrorism policy.

The Afridi-led convoy is aiming to reach Khairabad — which borders Punjab — by Oct 8, where the KP chief minister will announce the next plan of action.

After reaching Kohat’s Lachi tehsil on Monday night, CM Afridi said while addressing PTI supporters that this time, the party’s struggle was a long one that required endurance and sustained mobilisation, according to a statement issued by his office.

“We must not exhaust ourselves. Our struggle is a long one,” he said, adding that however, Oct 8 onwards, a “T20 match” would begin.

CM Afridi called upon the people of Kohat to turn out in overwhelming numbers, saying that the district should not allow any other district to outpace it in terms of participation in the protest.

“The message must go out clearly: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa belongs to Imran Khan, has belonged to Imran Khan, and will remain with Imran Khan,” the chief minister said. “I am a soldier of Imran Khan. The combined strength of the entire world cannot put a price on me, nor can it intimidate me,” he added.

He said the convoy would set out for Peshawar from University Chowk at 3pm.

Earlier in the day, Afridi also addressed PTI supporters in Karak, where the protesters arrived on Sunday night, railing against the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and criticising past military operations and drone attacks.

He also referred to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s remarks from a day earlier, wherein the latter called him “immature”.

He went on to recall Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz’s remarks on the terrorism threat to her province, adding: “Suppose, I say that [my province] does not have a threat from India, but from the other three provinces, will you consider me mature?”

The KP chief minister said, “If you deem it immature to speak about one’s province and people, then I have shown this immaturity yesterday, still do and will keep doing so.”

He contended that “wrong policies drafted behind closed doors were impacting all institutions”.

Expressing his patriotism for Pakistan, he said, “We also chant Pakistan zindabad; we stand up for the national anthem as well.”

But he added that future generations might not do so as there were attempts to “divide Pakistan and spread hatred”.

Insisting that his party was democratically presenting the public’s demands, Afridi warned that if the situation crossed all limits, neither would he be able to control the public “nor will anyone’s father have the courage” to do so.

He asserted that only those policies would be implemented that the people and the youth desire, and which were in the interests of the nation.

“We will not accept any decision taken behind closed doors that is against us, our province or Pakistan,” the chief minister added.
